cex-td-degenerate-thermometer-comparison.title: Degenerate thermometers can fail product comparison
cex-td-degenerate-thermometer-comparison.physical_scope: An abstract positive-energy thermometer model showing failure of T4 and the comparison hypothesis for products; it is not a measured thermometer or a claim about ordinary thermodynamic bodies.

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §IV.C, pp. 59–60
André Thess, The Lieb–Yngvason Machine: A didactical tool for the definition of entropy in classical thermodynamics, §2
Goddard, The second law of thermodynamics as variation on a theme of Carathéodory, §3

cex-td-degenerate-thermometer-comparison.statement: The one-system order relation $U\le U'$ on a degenerate thermometer state space $\Gamma=(0,\infty)$, together with the thermal equilibration operation described below, need not satisfy T4 or the comparison hypothesis on products. Consequently, a monotone entropy on the single-system space need not represent product accessibility.

cex-td-integrable-capacity-not-integer-p.title: Finite entropy integral does not force a heat-capacity power bound of order one or higher
cex-td-integrable-capacity-not-integer-p.physical_scope: A formal fixed-composition positive-temperature response chart used to refute an inference from integral convergence alone; it is not a measured material or a complete global bulk-family model.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete Chapter 4 lecture-note PDF, §4.5
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapter 2, §2.6.2

cex-td-integrable-capacity-not-integer-p.statement:
For a positive-temperature fixed-$V,n$ chart, write $\theta=T/T_*$. For a dimensionless real exponent $q\ge1$, the notation $C_V(T)=O(\theta^q)$ as $\theta\downarrow0$ means that there exist a constant $M>0$ measured in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and a dimensionless $\delta\in(0,1]$ such that $|C_V(T)|\le M\theta^q$ whenever $0<\theta<\delta$. Finite convergence of the entropy integral alone does not imply such a bound for any real $q\ge1$, even when the entropy has a finite limit and the local response-chart identities apply. The displayed branch is a formal chart calculation, not a claim that a particular substance realizes the chart.

The displayed entropy is $S^{\rm SI}$ in physical SI coordinates. For this constructed local model, choose the positive-amount open neighborhood stated here (or any positive neighborhood of the fixed amount, extending this entropy independently of amount) and let $O_c$ be the numerical preimage of that product patch under $\Phi_c(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)=(\hat U\,\mathrm J,\hat V\,\mathrm{m^3},\hat n\,\mathrm{mol})$. Declare $O_c$ as the model's local state-domain patch and set $S_c=S^{\rm SI}\circ\Phi_c$. The derivatives below are those of $S^{\rm SI}=S_c\circ\Phi_c^{-1}$ on $\Phi_c(O_c)$, exactly as in [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. This supplies the numerical-to-SI chart identification for the formal witness, with no assertion of a measured material or a global constitutive extension.

def-td-cross-type-reaction-network.title: Cross-type mixing and reaction network
def-td-cross-type-reaction-network.physical_scope: A declared family of allowed transitions between distinct tagged composition types, with finite catalyst chains and an explicit no-sinks condition; this definition does not claim a particular material network satisfies it.

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §§VI.A–VI.B

def-td-cross-type-reaction-network.statement:
A cross-type mixing and reaction network consists of a declared set $\mathcal G$ of tagged composition types and a state set $X_\Gamma$ for each type. Each state set comes with a fixed formal composition $\nu_\Gamma$, and its states satisfy $\nu(x)=\nu_\Gamma$ as in [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]]. These mathematical coefficients and their positive type weights are distinct from dimensioned material amounts. For physical channels the model additionally supplies endpoint quantity maps $U_\Gamma:X_\Gamma\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ and $n_\Gamma:X_\Gamma\to\mathbb R^r\,\mathrm{mol}$ in a declared finite species list, together with any separately tracked mechanical or external-field endpoint quantities. No identification of two distinct scaled tags is made.

For each channel $\alpha$ from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma'$, the model supplies sets $Z_\alpha$ of configurations, $\mathcal K_\alpha$ of protocol records, $\mathcal B_\alpha$ of outer-boundary records, and $\mathcal R_\alpha$ of transfer records, and equilibrium subsets and endpoint maps $\xi^-_\alpha:Z^-_\alpha\to X_\Gamma$, $\xi^+_\alpha:Z^+_\alpha\to X_{\Gamma'}$. A typed record is
$$P=(I,x^-,x^+,z,\kappa,b,r),$$
where $I=[t_0,t_1]$, $t_0<t_1$, is a finite time interval in seconds, $x^-\in X_\Gamma$, $x^+\in X_{\Gamma'}$, $z:I\to Z_\alpha$, $z(t_0)\in Z^-_\alpha$, $z(t_1)\in Z^+_\alpha$, $\xi^-_\alpha(z(t_0))=x^-$, $\xi^+_\alpha(z(t_1))=x^+$, $\kappa\in\mathcal K_\alpha$, $b\in\mathcal B_\alpha$, and $r\in\mathcal R_\alpha$. Transfer maps $Q_\alpha,W_{\mathrm{on},\alpha}:\mathcal R_\alpha\to\mathbb R\,\mathrm J$ and $N_\alpha:\mathcal R_\alpha\to\mathbb R^r\,\mathrm{mol}$ record heat, work and material transfer with declared signs; any tracked $\Delta K_{\mathrm{cm}}$ and $\Delta U_{\mathrm{ext}}$ are also joule-valued record maps. The channel specifies a balance predicate on this typed record set, or equivalently a balance map into a declared product of quantity spaces whose required value is zero, and a model-admitted subset satisfying that predicate. The predicate states the actual energy and material constraints of that channel; no balance law, physical admission or endpoint realizability follows from the tuple alone. For a fixed-constitution core closed channel, its endpoint embeddings, fields and admitted subset are exactly those of [[def-td-process-and-protocol]], with no material transfer and its stated kinetic/external restrictions. Other channels require their own adopted constraints. Define $(\Gamma,x)\mathcal R(\Gamma',y)$ exactly when an admitted channel record has those endpoints. No channel is inferred from separated composition.

For any permitted equal-formal-mass compound states $A,B$ of the network, define $A\prec B$ exactly when at least one admitted channel record has initial state $A$ and final state $B$; for named single types this is the relation $\mathcal R$ above. This is the exact relation supplied to [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], not a separate abstract order that enlarges or restricts the channel edges. Its extension to finite tagged products and common spectators is governed by the adopted A1–A6 conditions below. Thus every edge in a decorated chain is precisely an admitted channel transition. This identification is a declared model condition.

The network is **finite-factor closed** when its types admit the declared finite composition and positive scaling operations and each allowed channel respects the model’s stated conservation constraints. In addition, each channel must preserve the dimensionless formal mass $m$ of [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]]; this is the equal-coefficient-mass convention required by the mathematical chain-cost supplier, not a statement that formal mass is kilograms or moles. The common relation on all equal-formal-mass compounds satisfies A1–A6 of [[post-td-accessibility-a1-a6]], including consistency with spectators and stability. A decorated finite chain is exactly a finite sequence of such allowed transitions with a common catalyst and the real baseline-entropy edge costs in [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]].

For $\Gamma,\Gamma'$, let $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')\in\mathbb R\cup\{-\infty,+\infty\}$ be the infimum of those finite decorated-chain costs, with $+\infty$ if no witness exists and $-\infty$ if costs are unbounded below. The network has **no sinks** when, for every ordered type pair,

$$F(\Gamma,\Gamma')<+\infty\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad F(\Gamma',\Gamma)<+\infty.$$

No-sinks is an explicit property required of a network used in the global-offset theorem; it is not proved by this definition, and it is not asserted for every physical mixing or reaction. The definition permits the channel set to be empty; then the condition must still be checked rather than inferred.

def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain.title: Phase branches and coexistence domains
def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain.physical_scope: Model-specified phase branches of nonrelativistic macroscopic thermodynamic systems in positive-temperature, positive-composition, positive-amount charts; intensive scale invariance and same-tag homogeneity are separate branch assumptions, and no branch existence, stability, boundary smoothness, or universal phase rule is asserted.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, author-hosted complete lecture notes, Chapter 5, §§5.1.1–5.1.3
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Statistical Mechanics, §4.1 First-order phase transitions
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Statistical Mechanics, §4.2 Continuous phase transitions

def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain.statement:
Fix a constitution $c$ with $C\ge1$ named species and its equilibrium state domain $D_c\subseteq\mathbb R^{C+2}$ from [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]]. An interior composition is represented by

$$
x=(x_1,\ldots,x_{C-1})\in\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}:=\{x\in\mathbb R^{C-1}:x_i>0,\ \sum_{i=1}^{C-1}x_i<1\},
$$

with $x_C:=1-\sum_{i<C}x_i>0$; for $C=1$, $\mathbb R^0=\{0\}$ and $x_1=1$.

A **phase branch** $\alpha$ is model data consisting of an open chart $W_\alpha\subseteq(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\times\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}\times(0,\infty)$ with coordinates $(T,p,x,m)$ and a $C^1$ diffeomorphism $\sigma_\alpha:W_\alpha\to U_\alpha$ onto an open subset $U_\alpha\subseteq\mathbb R^{C+2}$ contained in the equilibrium state domain $D_c$. Here $T$ is in kelvins, $p$ is in pascals, $m$ is total amount in moles, and $C^1$ means continuous first coordinate derivatives as in [[def-ck-euclidean-maps-and-diffeomorphisms]]. The chart dimension is $C+2$, matching the ambient dimension of $D_c$. The map $\sigma_\alpha$ takes values in numerical state coordinates; its physical SI state map is explicitly $\chi_\alpha=\Phi_c\circ\sigma_\alpha$, where $\Phi_c$ is the numerical-to-SI unit map of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. Thus the physical amounts at this point are $n_j=m x_j$, and the numerical amount coordinates in $\sigma_\alpha$ are $n_j/(1\,\mathrm{mol})$. Derivative-defined physical state functions are evaluated on $\chi_\alpha(T,p,x,m)$, or equivalently pulled back along $\Phi_c$ to $\sigma_\alpha(T,p,x,m)$. At $\sigma_\alpha(T,p,x,m)$ in this precise pullback sense, the derivative-defined state functions of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]] give temperature $T$, pressure $p$, and mole fractions $x_j=n_j/m$; here $n_{\mathrm{tot}}:=\sum_{i=1}^C n_i=m$ uses the finite-sum convention of [[def-finite-sum]]. An **intensive phase branch** additionally has each derivative-defined chemical potential $\mu_j(T,p,x,m)$ independent of $m$ throughout $W_\alpha$; write its value as $\mu_j^\alpha(T,p,x)$. This scale invariance is an explicit constitutive model property, not a consequence of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]]. A valid local response chart and its inverse are as in [[def-td-response-functions]] and [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]. Existence of $W_\alpha$ or $\sigma_\alpha$ is a model premise, not a consequence of the equations of thermodynamics.

On a branch with a valid natural-variable chart, $G^\alpha$ denotes the Gibbs potential of [[def-td-legendre-potentials]] restricted to the branch. For a one-component branch with amount $m_\alpha>0$, define $g_\alpha:=G^\alpha/m_\alpha$, $s_\alpha:=S_\alpha/m_\alpha$, and $v_\alpha:=V_\alpha/m_\alpha$, in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$, $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$, respectively. These quotients need not be independent of amount, and $g_\alpha=\mu^\alpha$ is not assumed by this definition. Such an equality requires a separate same-tag homogeneity hypothesis on the branch.

A **phase mixture** of a finite list of branches is a feasible separated compound whose positive phase amounts $m_\alpha$ have fractions $\lambda_\alpha:=m_\alpha/\sum_\beta m_\beta>0$ with $\sum_\alpha\lambda_\alpha=1$. Its extensive coordinates and entropy are those supplied by [[post-td-bulk-additivity]] and [[post-td-concave-fundamental-entropy]], on the exact feasible set of [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. The mixture is in **coexistence** when it is an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint under the declared totals and permitted exchanges, as in [[post-td-entropy-maximum]]. This definition does not assert that a maximum exists, that all branches can exchange every coordinate, or that metastable states are global equilibria.

The bulk scaling postulate may send a material tag $c$ to a different tag $c^{(\lambda)}$. It therefore does not supply same-tag degree-one homogeneity of $G^\alpha$ or $U^\alpha$ on a phase branch. Any result using $g_\alpha=\mu^\alpha$ must state that additional hypothesis.

def-td-thermal-join.title: Thermal joins and thermal equivalence
def-td-thermal-join.physical_scope: The energy-summing contact operation for the declared simple-system family; it does not prescribe a temperature scale or guarantee that contact equilibrates any chosen pair.

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §IV.A
André Thess, The Lieb–Yngvason Machine: A didactical tool for the definition of entropy in classical thermodynamics, §§2–3

def-td-thermal-join.statement:
For the simple-compressible physical branch, a primitive label is a pair $i=(c_i,n^i)$ of constitution and fixed positive mole amounts. Its numerical state domain is exactly $\Gamma_i=\Gamma_{c_i,n^i}$ of [[def-td-equilibrium-state-domain]], with embedding $b_i(u,v)=(u,v,\hat n^i)\in D_{c_i}$. The unit map sends $(u,v)$ to $(u\,\mathrm J,v\,\mathrm{m^3})$; thus $u$ is the numerical value of the fixed internal energy, not a newly oriented energy coordinate. The underlying accessibility is the pullback of the admitted physical endpoint relation along $b_i$. Positive bulk scaling uses the declared scaling of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]], carries the mole vector to $\lambda n^i$, and retains the distinct scaled tag. More general work coordinates or formal thermometer examples require their own explicitly declared domain, coordinate unit map and endpoint relation; no identification with $D_c$ is supplied by this definition.

For two named simple-system types $i,j$ with energy/work coordinates $x=(u_i,v_i)$ and $y=(u_j,v_j)$, a thermal join is the model-declared compound state $J_{ij}(x,y)$ whose energy coordinate is $u_i+u_j$ and whose work coordinates retain the ordered pair $(v_i,v_j)$. Its join domain consists exactly of those tuples $(u,v_i,v_j)$ for which there are $u_i,u_j$ with $(u_i,v_i)$ and $(u_j,v_j)$ in the component domains and $u=u_i+u_j$. This is a tagged join state, distinct from the separated pair $(x,y)$, even when their total coordinates agree. The joined domain retains both work coordinates and has aggregate mole composition $n^i+n^j$ (in a common declared species list); it is not thereby a simple-compressible slice of one $D_c$. The contact model supplies its joined equilibrium endpoint space, endpoint coordinate map and admitted process relation. The contact model declares the pair encoding and join encoding to have the same aggregate composition and extends its accessibility relation to these two encodings; the contact axioms specify which such comparisons are admitted.

Write $x\sim_T y$ exactly when the pair $(x,y)$ and its join state $J_{ij}(x,y)$ are accessible in both directions under the declared contact operation. Here $\sim_T$ is a relation between states of the two named systems; it is not numerical equality of temperature. Nested joins use only the model’s declared reassociation and permutation identifications. The coordinate sum alone supplies no accessibility comparison.

def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs.title: Decorated finite-chain costs with catalysts

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §VI.B, Eqs. 6.6, 6.9, and 6.10, pp. 74–75
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapters 2 and 4, complete 607-page edition

def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs.statement:
Let $\mathcal G$ be a set of tagged system types closed under finite composition $T\times T'$ and positive scaling $tT$. Scaling is associative and acts componentwise on products: $s(tT)=(st)T$ and $t(T\times T')=(tT)\times(tT')$. Each type $T$ has a nonempty state set $X_T$ of finite tagged compounds, every state in $X_T$ is represented by the coefficient-map interpretation of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]] and has the fixed aggregate composition $\nu(a)=\nu_T$ of its declared type, using the amount-function interpretation in [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], and has total coefficient mass $m(T)=w_T\ge0$, and $\nu_{T\times T'}=\nu_T+\nu_{T'}$, $\nu_{tT}=t\nu_T$, with $m(T\times T')=m(T)+m(T')$ and $m(tT)=t\,m(T)$. Matching scalar masses alone do not identify aggregate composition. The entropy $\sigma_T:X_T\to\mathbb R$ is the finite additive extensive entropy from [[thm-tdmath-arbitrary-family-calibration]]; in particular $\sigma_{tT}(ta)=t\sigma_T(a)$.

Include the formal empty unit type $1$, with $X_1=\{*\}$, $m(1)=0$, $\sigma_1(*)=0$, $T\times1=T$, and $t1=1$. A transition edge from type $T$ to type $T'$ is a pair $a\in X_T$, $b\in X_{T'}$ such that the underlying equal-mass compounds satisfy $a\prec b$ under [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]]. Thus an edge can exist only when $m(T)=m(T')$. Its cost is the finite real number $\sigma_{T'}(b)-\sigma_T(a)$.

A decorated finite chain from $\Gamma$ to $\Gamma'$ consists of a catalyst type $C\in\mathcal G$, an integer $N\ge1$, types $T_0=\Gamma\times C,T_1,\ldots,T_N=\Gamma'\times C$, and states $a_k\in X_{T_k}$, $b_{k+1}\in X_{T_{k+1}}$ with an edge $a_k\prec b_{k+1}$ for every $0\le k<N$. Its cost is the finite real sum

$$c=\sum_{k=0}^{N-1}\bigl(\sigma_{T_{k+1}}(b_{k+1})-\sigma_{T_k}(a_k)\bigr).$$

Define $F(\Gamma,\Gamma')$ as the infimum of all such witness costs. Set $F=+\infty$ if there is no witness and $F=-\infty$ if the witness costs are unbounded below. The infimum is over real witness costs, so no subtraction of extended-real infima is used. Type permutations, reassociation, reversible identifications, and the identity $T\times1=T$ are part of the declared type structure. The cost identities and inequalities require a separate proof.

def-tdmath-diagonal-operator-model.title: Diagonal self-adjoint operator model

references.title: Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics (work in progress, dated 12 October 2026)
references.locator: Complete 635-page PDF retrieved; §§4.2–4.6, printed pp.192–217, for microcanonical, canonical, quantum trace and grand-canonical constructions.

def-tdmath-diagonal-operator-model.statement: Let $I$ be a finite or countably infinite set with a specified enumeration, let $E_i\in\mathbb R$, and let $\ell^2(I):=\{x:I\to\mathbb C:\sum_i|x_i|^2<\infty\}$ with inner product $\langle x,y\rangle=\sum_i x_i\overline{y_i}$, linear in the first variable. Write $u_i$ for the coordinate unit vector at $i$. The diagonal multiplication operator $H_E$ is the linear operator with domain $D(H_E):=\{x\in\ell^2(I):\sum_i|E_ix_i|^2<\infty\}$ and action $(H_Ex)_i:=E_ix_i$. [[lem-tdmath-diagonal-model-hilbert-and-domain]] proves completeness of the coefficient space, linearity and density of this domain, and linearity of the coordinate action before the Hilbert-space operator interpretation is used. Its domain is part of the operator data in the sense of [[def-unbounded-linear-operator-domain-and-graph]].

def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses.title: Forward-sector hypotheses for a simple state domain

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §§III.A–III.B
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapters 2 and 4, complete 607-page edition

def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses.statement:
Let $P$ be a set of primitive type labels. A formal type $\Gamma$ records a finitely supported amount function $\nu_\Gamma:P\to\mathbb R_{\ge0}$, not identically zero. Primitive generators have their unit amount function. Positive scaling, separated product, and thermal-join constructors retain distinct formal tags and obey

$$\nu_{s\Gamma}=s\nu_\Gamma,\qquad \nu_{\Gamma\otimes\Gamma'}=\nu_\Gamma+\nu_{\Gamma'}\qquad(s>0).$$

Separated and joined types are distinct constructors even when their amount functions agree. Permutation, reassociation, and scaled-splitting conventions preserve the amount function. Define the positive **bookkeeping weight** $w_\Gamma:=\sum_{p\in P}\nu_\Gamma(p)$, a finite sum over support. Thus $w_{s\Gamma}=s w_\Gamma$ and every product or join has weight $w_\Gamma+w_{\Gamma'}$. The optional empty unit has zero amount function and weight zero; it is represented only by the empty compound, not as a simple chart. These are formal amounts, not masses in kilograms or an empirical conservation law. The functions and pointwise operations use [[def-function-space]]; their finite-support convention and finite sums are those of [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]] and [[lem-tdmath-compound-mass-well-defined]].

Let $I$ index the declared family of simple types $\Gamma_i$. For each simple type $\Gamma$ in that family, let $n_\Gamma\ge1$ and let $\Gamma\subset\mathbb R^{n_\Gamma+1}$ be nonempty, open and convex, with coordinates $x=(u,v)$. The notation for a type and its chart is shared, but each state has a distinct raw tag $(\Gamma,x)$. Scaled charts are distinct tagged copies $s\Gamma=\{sx:x\in\Gamma\}$ with coordinate transport $x\mapsto sx$; transported raw tags remain distinct from the original raw tags. Let $e_{(\Gamma,x)}$ be the unit point mass from [[def-tdmath-tagged-scalable-compound]]. The represented state is

$$\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x):=w_\Gamma e_{(\Gamma,x)},\qquad m(\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x))=w_\Gamma.$$

Write $\mathsf{J}(x):=\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ when $x$ already carries its type tag. All state notation in this framework's compound comparisons, including a bare $x$, denotes $\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$; a raw unit point mass is always written $e_{(\Gamma,x)}$. A separated pair is addition of represented states, not a unit product tag. Nonnegative multiples are pointwise and zero terms are omitted. For an encoded compound $c$, its aggregate composition is the finite amount function

$$\nu(c):=\sum_{(\Gamma,x)\in\operatorname{supp}(c)}\frac{c(\Gamma,x)}{w_\Gamma}\nu_\Gamma;\qquad m(c)=\sum_{p\in P}\nu(c)(p).$$

Fix the formal interpretation $\Pi(c)$ as the finite separated preparation whose factor at each nonzero raw tag $(\Gamma,x)$ is the amount $c(\Gamma,x)/w_\Gamma$ of that typed state, using the declared coordinate scaling transport. The accessibility relation on coefficient maps is the pullback of the declared relation on these preparations. Merging or splitting repeated copies of the same preparation is reversible; permutation and reassociation preserve the preparation. Thus $\Pi(\mathsf{J}_{s\Gamma}(sx))$ and $\Pi(s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x))$ are the same declared scaled preparation and yield

$$\mathsf{J}_{s\Gamma}(sx)\sim s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x),$$

although their raw point masses have different tags and are not equal. This reversible transport commutes with finite composition, nested type constructors, and scaled splitting. It is part of the precise formal scaling interpretation, not a deduction about physical accessibility from coordinate multiplication. A physical use must adopt the stated preparation maps and accessibility assumptions; fixed-composition models compare only preparations with the same $\nu$, while a declared channel model may additionally compare different compositions of equal $m$.

A comparison $A\prec B$ is defined only when $m(A)=m(B)$, as in the coefficient-map supplier. Write $A\sim B$ when both directions hold, and $A\prec\prec B$ when only the forward direction holds. On any fixed simple type, dividing every represented state by the same positive constant $w_\Gamma$ gives its unit-point-mass comparison. Positive scaling and its inverse preserve and reflect order; whenever the required CH and reference hypotheses hold, the unit-state entropy theorem applies after that normalization. If $S$ represents unit-point-mass comparisons, the entropy of a represented state is $w_\Gamma S(x)$ and the entropy of a finite sum $\sum_j t_j\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x_j)$ is $\sum_j t_j w_\Gamma S(x_j)$. No independent rescaling across different types is assumed without a calibrator.

The common relation satisfies A1–A6 on all equal-mass finite compounds: (A1) reflexivity; (A2) transitivity; (A3) if $A\prec B$, then $A+C\prec B+C$ for every compound $C$; (A4) if $A\prec B$, then $tA\prec tB$ for every $t>0$; (A5) $t\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ is equivalent to $s\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)+(t-s)\mathsf{J}_\Gamma(x)$ for $t>0$ and $0<s<t$, with the reversible scaled-copy transport above; (A6) for equal-mass $A,B$, fixed positive equal-mass spectators $Z_0,Z_1$, and every sequence $\epsilon_n>0$ decreasing to zero, $A+\epsilon_n Z_0\prec B+\epsilon_n Z_1$ for all $n$ implies $A\prec B$. These are hypotheses, not conclusions. No comparison hypothesis is included here.

For each $i$ and $x\in\Gamma_i$, define the forward sector $A_x:=\{y\in\Gamma_i:\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(x)\prec\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(y)\}$. The simple-domain assumptions are: (A7) for $x,y\in\Gamma_i$ and $0<t<1$, the encoded compound $t\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(x)+(1-t)\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(y)$ compares to $\mathsf{J}_{\Gamma_i}(tx+(1-t)y)$; both have bookkeeping mass $w_{\Gamma_i}$, and convexity puts the recombined coordinate in the chart; (S1) each $x$ has a strict successor; (S2) $A_x$ has exactly one supporting hyperplane at $x$, expressible as $u-u_x+P_i(x)\cdot(v-v_x)=0$ with a finite-valued slope map $P_i:\Gamma_i\to\mathbb R^{n_i}$, and $P_i$ is locally Lipschitz; (S3) the boundary of $A_x$ relative to $\Gamma_i$ is arcwise connected. A supporting hyperplane means that $A_x$ lies in one of its closed half-spaces and meets the plane at $x$. The affine hull is the smallest affine subspace containing a set; relative interior is interior in that affine hull. Closure and boundary are taken in the indicated affine hull or in $\Gamma_i$, as named; boundary is closure intersected with closure of the complement in that relative topology.

This definition imposes no physical interpretation, units, or empirical claim. A contact theorem that uses joins must separately assume that each join is a simple domain satisfying these same forward-sector hypotheses.

def-tdmath-measure-integral.statement: A measure space is a triple $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ where $\Sigma$ contains $\varnothing,X$ and is closed under complements and countable unions (a $\sigma$-algebra) of subsets of $X$ and $\mu:\Sigma\to[0,\infty]$ is countably additive with $\mu(\varnothing)=0$. A measurable function $f:X\to[-\infty,\infty]$ has measurable inverse images of Borel sets, where $[-\infty,\infty]$ has its order topology: finite open intervals and the endpoint neighborhoods $[-\infty,a)$ and $(a,\infty]$ form a basis. Its Borel sigma-algebra is generated by these open sets. A complex-valued function is measurable exactly when its finite real and imaginary parts are measurable, equivalently for the usual Borel structure of $\mathbb C$. Almost-everywhere assertions mean outside a measurable $\mu$-null set; completeness of $\mu$ is not assumed. Nonnegative extended addition uses $a+\infty=\infty+a=\infty$ for $a\in[0,\infty]$; positive scalars multiply $\infty$ to $\infty$, while $0\cdot\infty=0$. Signed expressions $\infty-\infty$ remain undefined and are not used in signed integrals. A nonnegative simple function has the form $s=\sum_{j=1}^m c_j\mathbf1_{A_j}$ with finitely many disjoint $A_j\in\Sigma$ and finite $c_j\ge0$. Define $c\mu(A)=+\infty$ if $c>0$ and $\mu(A)=+\infty$, define $0\cdot\infty:=0$, and define the finite sum of these extended nonnegative terms to be $+\infty$ if any term is $+\infty$ and otherwise the real finite sum of [[def-finite-sum]]. Then $\int s\,d\mu:=\sum_j c_j\mu(A_j)$; using canonical level sets $\{s=c\}$ makes this value representation-independent. For measurable $f\ge0$, define $\int f\,d\mu:=\sup\{\int s\,d\mu: s\text{ is simple and }0\le s\le f\}$, using [[def-complete-ordered-field]] for a bounded set of finite values and setting the supremum to $+\infty$ when the values are unbounded or one is infinite. A real measurable $f$ is integrable when $\int|f|\,d\mu<\infty$, and then $\int f:=\int f^+-\int f^-$, where $f^+=\max(f,0)$ and $f^-:=\max(-f,0)$. Complex integrability and integration are defined by integrable real and imaginary parts.

def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-referen.title: Poisson Configuration Reference

references.title: H.-O. Georgii and H. Zessin, Large deviations and the maximum entropy principle for marked point random fields
references.locator: Section 2.3, printed p.184 / PDF p.7, Poisson reference and specific entropy

def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-referen.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and fix an integer dimension $d\geq1$. For $i\in\mathbb Z^d$, let $C_i=i+[0,1)^d$. These are left-closed, right-open cells. For every $x\in\mathbb R^d$, [[lem-integer-part]] supplies the unique integers $i_j$ with $i_j\le x_j<i_j+1$, so $x$ belongs to exactly one $C_i$. The cells are Borel products of closed/open ray intersections and have volume one by [[thm-lebesgue-measure-of-a-box-of-every-kind]], whose statement covers this face convention. A finite configuration in $C_i$ is a finite subset of distinct points. Encode it by its cardinality $n\in\mathbb N_0$ and its uniquely lexicographically increasing list of local coordinates $(x_1-i,\ldots,x_n-i)\in([0,1)^d)^n$. Pad the code after its first $n$ coordinates with the zero vector. For fixed $n$, the strictly increasing lists form a Borel subset of $([0,1]^d)^n$, since lexicographic strict order is a finite union of coordinate-equality and coordinate-inequality conditions. Thus all codes form a Borel subset of $\mathbb N_0\times([0,1]^d)^{\mathbb N}$. Each factor $[0,1]^d$ is Polish as a closed subspace of complete $\mathbb R^d$ with a countable dense rational grid; $\mathbb N_0$ with its discrete metric is Polish. The ambient space is Polish by [[cor-countable-products-and-g-delta-subspaces-of-polish-spaces-are-polish]] (and is completely metrized by [[lem-standard-complete-metric-on-a-countable-product]]), so [[lem-borel-subspaces-admit-polish-presentations]] makes the cell space $E_i$ standard Borel. By [[lem-tdmath-counts-generate-configuration-sigma]], its sigma-algebra is generated by the counts $N_B$ for Borel $B\subseteq C_i$.

For $\lambda>0$, give a cell configuration with $n$ points probability $e^{-\lambda}\lambda^n/n!$ for its count. The probabilities sum to one by the exponential power series and addition formula. Conditional on count $n$, take the $n$-fold product of normalized Lebesgue measure on $C_i$, restrict it to the complement of the collision diagonals, and push it forward by lexicographic sorting. The product exists by the finite product-measure theorem; each collision diagonal is null by Tonelli and the fact that Lebesgue measure gives every singleton measure zero, so the restricted measure still has mass one. Sorting is Borel on the finitely many permutation regions of the no-collision set. This defines a law $\pi_{i,\lambda}$ on $E_i$; for $n=0$, use the empty product and the empty configuration. Let $\Omega=\prod_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}E_i$ with its product cylinder sigma-algebra. The product sigma-algebra is generated by the cell-coordinate sigma-algebras, each generated by counts on Borel subsets of its bounded cell by [[lem-tdmath-counts-generate-configuration-sigma]]. Conversely every bounded-region count is a finite sum of these cell counts, since a bounded set meets finitely many cells. Thus the product cylinder sigma-algebra is exactly the sigma-algebra generated by all bounded-Borel count maps. For each $\lambda>0$, $Q_\lambda$ denotes the unique probability on $\Omega$ whose finite cell marginals are the products of the corresponding $\pi_{i,\lambda}$. Existence and uniqueness follow from [[thm-kolmogorov-extension-for-standard-borel-coordinate-spaces]]. In particular every translation $T_x$ is measurable since $N_A(T_x\omega)=N_{A-x}(\omega)$. The unit-intensity reference is $Q:=Q_1$.

Identify each $\omega\in\Omega$ with the simple locally finite counting measure obtained by uniting its finite cell configurations. For a bounded Borel set $A\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, write $N_A(\omega)=\omega(A)$ and $|A|$ for its Lebesgue measure. Define translation by $T_x\omega(A)=\omega(A-x)$ for $x\in\mathbb R^d$. The next item proves that under $Q_\lambda$, counts in disjoint bounded Borel sets are independent Poisson random variables with means $\lambda|A|$ and that $Q_\lambda$ is translation invariant. This item is a mathematical reference construction and makes no physical claim.

ex-td-clapeyron-linear-branches.title: A two-branch Gibbs model with a positive Clapeyron slope
ex-td-clapeyron-linear-branches.physical_scope: A constructed pair of one-component Gibbs charts satisfying the same-tag, exchange, and reversible-heat assumptions of the local Clapeyron theorem; the constants are illustrative and are not observations.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, author-hosted complete lecture notes, §§5.1.1–5.1.2
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Statistical Mechanics, §4.1 First-order phase transitions

ex-td-clapeyron-linear-branches.statement:
Fix $T_0=300\,\mathrm K$, $p_0=10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}$, $g_0=1\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$, $c>0$ in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, and $\kappa>0$ in $\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}Pa^{-1}}$. On a common open chart define
$$
g_i(T,p)=g_0-s_i(T-T_0)-\frac{c}{2T_0}(T-T_0)^2+v_i(p-p_0)-\frac{\kappa}{2}(p-p_0)^2,
$$
for $i\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$, with $s_\alpha=2\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, $s_\beta=5\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, $v_\alpha=1.0\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$, and $v_\beta=4.0\times10^{-3}\,\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$. Set $G_i=n_i g_i$ and use the natural Gibbs assignments $S_i=-\partial_TG_i$, $V_i=\partial_pG_i$, $\mu_i=\partial_{n_i}G_i$, and $U_i=G_i+TS_i-pV_i$. Thus same-tag homogeneity is explicit. Assume the constructed model stipulates an attained coexistence endpoint with bilateral energy, volume, and species exchange, and a reversible $\alpha\to\beta$ conversion in contact with an ideal thermal reservoir at $T_0$. The reversible conversion is a record of the complete finite isolated compound comprising converted phases, the fixed-temperature reservoir, work stores and all auxiliaries, with equilibrium endpoints and additive component entropy. Every component other than the converted phases and reservoir has zero entropy change, and the reservoir change is $-Q/T_0$. These are the exact additional entropy premises of the local Clapeyron theorem. These parameters and endpoint assumptions are model inputs, not empirical claims.

ex-td-nonzero-isothermal-work-loop.title: Nonzero pressure work around a closed model cycle
ex-td-nonzero-isothermal-work-loop.physical_scope: Constructed smooth concave positive-temperature chart and an idealized quasistatic piston cycle at fixed composition; the work and heat values are model calculations, not reported observations.

references.title: Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §2.7
Jeremy Tatum, Heat and Thermodynamics, §12.5, Summary, Maxwell Relations, and Gibbs-Helmholtz Relations

ex-td-nonzero-isothermal-work-loop.statement:
Fix a material constitution and amount $n$ and stipulate, on $U>0$ and $0<V<1/b$, the entropy chart

$$S(U,V)=C\ln(U/U_*)+aV-\frac{ab}{2}V^2+S_0,$$

where $C>0$ is in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $U_*>0$ is in joules, $a>0$ is in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, $b>0$ is in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, and $S_0$ is in $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. Consider a piecewise-C1 quasistatic cycle with isotherms $T_1>T_2>0$ and volumes $0<V_1<V_2<1/b$, joined by isochoric legs. The ideal frictionless piston load tracks the equilibrium pressure, controlled heat exchange is permitted along the path, and no other work coordinate acts. The calculation shows that the pressure-work integral is not an endpoint increment.

The displayed entropy is $S^{\rm SI}$ in physical SI coordinates. For this constructed local model, choose the positive-amount open neighborhood stated here (or any positive neighborhood of the fixed amount, extending this entropy independently of amount) and let $O_c$ be the numerical preimage of that product patch under $\Phi_c(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)=(\hat U\,\mathrm J,\hat V\,\mathrm{m^3},\hat n\,\mathrm{mol})$. Declare $O_c$ as the model's local state-domain patch and set $S_c=S^{\rm SI}\circ\Phi_c$. The derivatives below are those of $S^{\rm SI}=S_c\circ\Phi_c^{-1}$ on $\Phi_c(O_c)$, exactly as in [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. This supplies the numerical-to-SI chart identification for the formal witness, with no assertion of a measured material or a global constitutive extension.

ex-td-phase-rule-single-component.title: One component in two phases has one regular equation-set degree of freedom
ex-td-phase-rule-single-component.physical_scope: A constructed pair of smooth one-component Gibbs charts; the example verifies the regular equation-set rank and dimension only, and does not assert a stable or realized coexistence endpoint.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, author-hosted complete lecture notes, §5.1.1
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Statistical Mechanics, §4.1 First-order phase transitions

ex-td-phase-rule-single-component.statement:
Let $C=1$, $P=2$, and $R=0$. Fix $T_0=300\,\mathrm K$ and $p_0=10^5\,\mathrm{Pa}$, and take a common open chart around $(T_0,p_0)$. On it define the branch Gibbs potentials per mole
$$
g_1(T,p)=g_0-s_0(T-T_0)-\frac{c}{2T_0}(T-T_0)^2+v_1(p-p_0)-\frac{\kappa}{2}(p-p_0)^2,\qquad g_2(T,p)=g_0-s_0(T-T_0)-\frac{c}{2T_0}(T-T_0)^2+v_2(p-p_0)-\frac{\kappa}{2}(p-p_0)^2,
$$
where $g_0$ is in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$, $s_0,c>0$ are in $\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, $v_1,v_2>0$ are distinct molar volumes in $\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$, and $\kappa>0$ is in $\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}Pa^{-1}}$. Set $G_i=n_i g_i$ with natural Gibbs assignments $S_i=-\partial_TG_i$, $V_i=\partial_pG_i$, and $\mu_i=\partial_{n_i}G_i$; define $U_i=G_i+TS_i-pV_i$. The derivative-defined chemical potentials are $\mu_i=g_i$, and they agree at $(T_0,p_0)$. This is a candidate equation-map solution, not a claim of entropy-maximizing coexistence.

The constructed branch's local physical state map is $\chi:(T,p,n)\mapsto(U,V,n)$ (using the positive amount and interior composition coordinates displayed here). On the inverse patch verified below, define its numerical domain $O_c=\Phi_c^{-1}(\chi(\mathcal O))$ and declare this patch to be the local model's $D_c$ patch, where $\Phi_c(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)=(\hat U\,\mathrm J,\hat V\,\mathrm{m^3},\hat n\,\mathrm{mol})$ is the unit map of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. Define the numerical entropy by $S_c=S^{\rm SI}\circ\Phi_c$, with $S^{\rm SI}$ supplied by the Gibbs assignments through this inverse. Thus the displayed derivatives are derivatives in physical SI coordinates on $\Phi_c(O_c)$; the model patch is not an empirical claim about an independently specified material domain.

ex-td-positive-log-contact-witness.title: Positive logarithmic contact model as a consistency witness
ex-td-positive-log-contact-witness.physical_scope: A calculated mathematical model showing compatibility of the stated accessibility and contact assumptions for positive-coordinate systems; it is not an experiment or evidence that real materials obey the assumptions.

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §§III.B–IV.A
André Thess, The Lieb–Yngvason Machine: A didactical tool for the definition of entropy in classical thermodynamics, §§2–4

ex-td-positive-log-contact-witness.statement:
Take finitely many tagged simple types $i$, each with positive dimensionless coordinates $u>0,v>0$ (numerical energy and work coordinates relative to fixed units). Choose constants $c_i,r_i>0$, reference values $u_{\star,i},v_{\star,i}>0$, and $b_i\in\mathbb R$, and define

$$s_i(u,v)=c_i\log\frac{u}{u_{\star,i}}+r_i\log\frac{v}{v_{\star,i}}+b_i.$$

For a scaled tag $t i$, set its coefficients to $tc_i,tr_i,tb_i$ and its reference coordinates to $t u_{\star,i},t v_{\star,i}$, so $s_{ti}(tu,tv)=t\,s_i(u,v)$. On finite separated compounds define the relation by nondecrease of the sum of the constituent entropies. For a thermal join of $i,j$, define the joined entropy at $(U,v_i,v_j)$ as the maximum of $s_i(u_i,v_i)+s_j(u_j,v_j)$ over $u_i,u_j>0$ with $u_i+u_j=U$, and define contact equilibrium by equality of the pair entropy with this maximum. For nested joins, use the same maximum construction recursively.

This formal model explicitly declares each equilibrium endpoint domain to be the stated positive numerical orthant, with endpoint coordinate map the identity and accessibility the entropy-sum relation above. Its fixed unit map assigns $U=u(1\,\mathrm J)$ and each work coordinate $W_a=v_aw_a$ for a fixed positive unit $w_a$; this bookkeeping supplies no material realization. Each primitive tag has a fixed formal composition, while the joined endpoint space is the positive orthant in summed energy and retained work coordinates with the summed composition. A scaled copy transports these coordinates and that composition and retains its distinct tag, exactly as in the declared join interface. This provides a nondegenerate consistency witness for the order, geometric, contact, T5, and C1 assumptions on this positive-coordinate family. It supplies no measured parameter values or empirical claim.

ex-td-reactive-phase-rule-three-componen.title: A regular two-phase three-species reaction model
ex-td-reactive-phase-rule-three-componen.physical_scope: A constructed smooth local two-phase Gibbs model with one formal internal reaction, used to verify the local equation-map nonsingular-minor hypothesis only; no stable or realized coexistence claim, empirical system, or chemical data are made.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, author-hosted complete lecture notes, §5.1.1
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Statistical Mechanics, §4.1 First-order phase transitions

ex-td-reactive-phase-rule-three-componen.statement:
Take $C=3$ species and $P=2$ phases. Write $x_3:=1-x_1-x_2$, and center the open composition charts at $x_1=x_2=x_3=1/3$. Fix $T_0>0$, $p_0>0$, $s_0,c,v_0,\kappa,q>0$, and $\eta=1\,\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}}$. The parameters have units $s_0,c\in\mathrm{J\,mol^{-1}K^{-1}}$, $v_0\in\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$, $\kappa\in\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}Pa^{-1}}$, and $q\in\mathrm{m^3\,mol^{-1}}$. For $\gamma\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$, set $a_\alpha=2\eta$, $a_\beta=\eta$, $q_\alpha=0$, and $q_\beta=q$, and define molar Gibbs potentials
$$
g^\gamma(T,p,x)=-s_0(T-T_0)-\frac{c}{2T_0}(T-T_0)^2+v_0(p-p_0)-\frac{\kappa}{2}(p-p_0)^2+\frac{a_\gamma}{2}(x_1^2+x_2^2)-\frac{a_\gamma}{3}(x_1+x_2)+\frac{a_\gamma}{9}+q_\gamma(p-p_0)x_3.
$$
Set $G^\gamma=m_\gamma g^\gamma$ on each fixed-tag branch and adopt the natural Gibbs assignments $S=-G_T$, $V=G_p$, and $\mu_j=G_{n_j}$, with $U=G+TS-pV$. These smooth charts are scale-invariant in amount. Near the centered point the volumes are positive, and the $(U,V)$ chart Jacobian at fixed composition and amount is nonsingular: $U_T=m_\gamma c$, $V_p=-m_\gamma\kappa$, and $V_T=0$ there, so its determinant is $-m_\gamma^2c\kappa\ne0$. The reaction vector is $\nu=(-1,-1/2,1)^{\mathsf T}$, of rank $R=1$. At $(T_0,p_0,x_1,x_2)=(T_0,p_0,1/3,1/3)$, both phases have $\mu^\gamma=(0,0,0)$, so the phase-equality equations and reaction affinity vanish.

The constructed branch's local physical state map is $\chi:(T,p,n)\mapsto(U,V,n)$ (using the positive amount and interior composition coordinates displayed here). On the inverse patch verified below, define its numerical domain $O_c=\Phi_c^{-1}(\chi(\mathcal O))$ and declare this patch to be the local model's $D_c$ patch, where $\Phi_c(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)=(\hat U\,\mathrm J,\hat V\,\mathrm{m^3},\hat n\,\mathrm{mol})$ is the unit map of [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. Define the numerical entropy by $S_c=S^{\rm SI}\circ\Phi_c$, with $S^{\rm SI}$ supplied by the Gibbs assignments through this inverse. Thus the displayed derivatives are derivatives in physical SI coordinates on $\Phi_c(O_c)$; the model patch is not an empirical claim about an independently specified material domain.

ex-td-response-chart-failure.title: A smooth chart with no isothermal pressure inverse
ex-td-response-chart-failure.physical_scope: Constructed local concave entropy chart at fixed composition, used only to show failure of a response-coordinate inverse; it is not a measured material equation of state or a complete bulk-family model.

references.title: Daniel Arovas, Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §2.10.5

ex-td-response-chart-failure.statement:
Fix the amount of substance and stipulate the local entropy representative

$$S(U,V)=C\ln(U/U_*)+aV+S_0$$

on the open domain $U>0$, $V>0$, where $C>0$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, $U_*>0$ has units joules, $a>0$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,m^{-3}}$, and $S_0$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$. This chart is finite, C2, concave, and has $S_U>0$. It illustrates that a smooth positive-temperature chart need not admit pressure as a local coordinate at fixed temperature.

The displayed entropy is $S^{\rm SI}$ in physical SI coordinates. For this constructed local model, choose the positive-amount open neighborhood stated here (or any positive neighborhood of the fixed amount, extending this entropy independently of amount) and let $O_c$ be the numerical preimage of that product patch under $\Phi_c(\hat U,\hat V,\hat n)=(\hat U\,\mathrm J,\hat V\,\mathrm{m^3},\hat n\,\mathrm{mol})$. Declare $O_c$ as the model's local state-domain patch and set $S_c=S^{\rm SI}\circ\Phi_c$. The derivatives below are those of $S^{\rm SI}=S_c\circ\Phi_c^{-1}$ on $\Phi_c(O_c)$, exactly as in [[def-td-temperature-pressure-chemical-potential]]. This supplies the numerical-to-SI chart identification for the formal witness, with no assertion of a measured material or a global constitutive extension.

ex-td-vdw-positive-slope.title: A positive-slope segment in the reduced van der Waals model
ex-td-vdw-positive-slope.physical_scope: An exact derivative calculation in the dimensionless reduced van der Waals model below its model critical temperature; no real-fluid measurement or universal equation of state is asserted.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, author-hosted complete lecture notes, §5.1.1
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Statistical Mechanics, §4.1 First-order phase transitions

ex-td-vdw-positive-slope.statement:
Adopt the reduced van der Waals equation as a phenomenological model:
$$
p(v,t)=\frac{8t}{3v-1}-\frac{3}{v^2},\qquad v>\frac13,\quad t>0,
$$
where $p=P/P_c$, $v=V/V_c$, and $t=T/T_c$ use positive model scales $P_c,V_c,T_c$. Define a model critical point by the simultaneous isothermal conditions $\partial_vp=\partial_v^2p=0$ in this domain. The equation is a model premise; its extension to liquid-like densities is not a universal physical law.

ex-tdmath-hard-core-zero-beta.title: A hard core remains at zero inverse temperature

references.title: H.-O. Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction
references.locator: Section 2, printed pp.172–174 / PDF pp.2–4: finite-volume Boltzmann weights assign zero weight to forbidden infinite-energy configurations for positive inverse temperature. The retained-admissibility zero-parameter convention is supplied by [[thm-tdmath-retained-hard-zero-beta-limit]], with the finite calculation proved below; Theorem 4 on printed p.177 allows a nonnegative multiplier; this finite retained-exclusion calculation is proved locally and does not invoke a positive-temperature LDP at zero.

ex-tdmath-hard-core-zero-beta.statement:
In one spatial dimension, let $\phi(x)=+\infty$ for $|x|<a$ and $0$ otherwise, with $a>0$. On an interval $[0,L]$, define the beta-zero weight by retaining the forbidden-pair exclusion as in [[thm-tdmath-retained-hard-zero-beta-limit]]. If $L>a$, the two-particle canonical partition is
$$Z(L,2;0)=\frac{(L-a)^2}{2},$$
while the unrestricted ideal-gas value is $L^2/2$. Thus the retained hard-core beta-zero ensemble is not the Poisson ideal gas.

ex-tdmath-pure-state-versus-average-entr.title: Pure-state entropy and entropy of a dephased average

references.title: Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
references.locator: Complete 635-page lecture notes retrieved and read; §§4.2–4.6, pp.192–217, ensembles, microcanonical phase space, quantum density matrices, and traces.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete author-hosted lecture text
references.locator: Complete author-hosted HTML chapter read; §§1.2–1.4, finite canonical and microcanonical ensemble conventions.

ex-tdmath-pure-state-versus-average-entr.statement: Use $\mathcal H=\mathbb C^2$ with $\langle z,w\rangle=z_1\overline{w_1}+z_2\overline{w_2}$, linear in the first argument, and $u_1=(1,0)$, $u_2=(0,1)$. Choose real $E_1\ne E_2$ and define the self-adjoint energy operator $A(z_1,z_2)=(E_1z_1,E_2z_2)$. Fix $\hbar>0$, set $U_tu_j=e^{-iE_jt/\hbar}u_j$, and define $P_jz=\langle z,u_j\rangle u_j$, $\rho_t=U_t\rho U_t^*$ and $\bar\rho_T=T^{-1}\int_0^T\rho_t\,dt$. Let $\psi=(u_1+u_2)/\sqrt2$, $\rho=|\psi\rangle\langle\psi|$. Define the finite-dimensional entropy of a density matrix with eigenvalues $p_i$ as $S(\rho)=-k_B\sum_i p_i\log p_i$, with $0\log0=0$ and fixed $k_B>0$. Every instantaneous unitary state $\rho_t$ is pure and has entropy zero. The Cesàro states converge to $\rho_{\rm diag}=(P_1+P_2)/2$, whose entropy is $k_B\log2$. In fact $S(\bar\rho_T)\to k_B\log2$, whereas $T^{-1}\int_0^T S(\rho_t)\,dt=0$ for every $T$. Entropy of the averaged state and average instantaneous entropy are distinct quantities.

ex-tdmath-unit-poisson-reference-informa.title: The Reference Has Zero Specific Relative Entropy
ex-tdmath-unit-poisson-reference-informa.statement: Take $P=Q$, the unit-intensity Poisson configuration reference. This gives the zero-information baseline for the A-page specific relative entropy.

lem-tdmath-convex-function-local-lipschi.title: Finite convex functions are locally Lipschitz

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §III.C
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.1 and 7.2–7.3, complete 607-page edition

lem-tdmath-convex-function-local-lipschi.statement: Let $U\subset\mathbb R^d$ be open and convex, and let $f:U\to\mathbb R$ be finite and convex, meaning $f((1-t)x+ty)\le(1-t)f(x)+tf(y)$ for every $x,y\in U$ and $t\in[0,1]$. For every $x_0\in U$, there are a neighborhood $V$ of $x_0$ and $L<\infty$ such that $|f(x)-f(y)|\le L\|x-y\|$ for all $x,y\in V$. The same conclusion holds for finite concave functions by applying the result to $-f$.

lem-tdmath-counts-generate-configuration.title: Counts Generate the Sigma-Algebra of Finite Configurations

references.title: H.-O. Georgii and H. Zessin, Large deviations and the maximum entropy principle for marked point random fields
references.locator: Section 2.1, printed pp.181–182 / PDF pp.4–5, configuration sigma algebra generated by counting variables and its Borel configuration-space presentation

lem-tdmath-counts-generate-configuration.statement:
Let $C=[0,1)^d$ for an integer $d\geq1$. Let $\mathsf C_f(C)$ be the set of finite subsets of $C$, represented by their cardinality $n$ and their uniquely lexicographically increasing list $(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$. Give this set the Borel structure of the countable disjoint union of the Borel subspaces of $C^n$ consisting of strictly increasing lists. For each Borel $B\subseteq C$, let $N_B(\eta)=\#(\eta\cap B)$. Then
$$\mathcal B(\mathsf C_f(C))=\sigma\{N_B:B\in\mathcal B(C)\}.$$

lem-tdmath-diagonal-self-adjointness.title: Diagonal multiplication is self-adjoint

references.title: Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics (work in progress, dated 12 October 2026)
references.locator: Complete 635-page PDF retrieved; §§4.2–4.6, printed pp.192–217, for microcanonical, canonical, quantum trace and grand-canonical constructions.

lem-tdmath-diagonal-self-adjointness.statement: For the diagonal model [[def-tdmath-diagonal-operator-model]], the operator $H_E$ is densely defined and self-adjoint on $\ell^2(I)$.

lem-tdmath-forward-spectator-cancellatio.title: Spectator cancellation without comparison completeness

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, Theorem 2.1 and §III.C
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.1 and 7.2–7.3, complete 607-page edition

lem-tdmath-forward-spectator-cancellatio.statement: Under A1–A6 of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], for compounds $A,B$ with $m(A)=m(B)$ and every finite spectator compound $C$, $A+C\prec B+C$ if and only if $A\prec B$. Consequently, for finite-support signed maps $u,v$ of equal total coefficient, define $u\preceq_s v$ by $(v-u)^-\prec(v-u)^+$. This relation is well-defined, agrees with $\prec$ on nonnegative maps, is invariant under adding a common signed map, is transitive, and is closed under addition of two comparisons. No comparison hypothesis is used.

lem-tdmath-integral-zero-uniqueness.title: Zero-start integral inequality

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §III.C
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Appendix 9.9, complete 607-page edition

lem-tdmath-integral-zero-uniqueness.statement: Let $L\ge0$, $T>0$, and let $f:[0,T]\to[0,\infty)$ be continuous. If $f(t)\le L\int_0^t f(s)\,ds$ for every $t\in[0,T]$, then $f(t)=0$ for every $t\in[0,T]$.

lem-tdmath-relative-boundary-support.title: Supporting hyperplanes at relative boundary points

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §III.C
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, §§4.1 and 7.2–7.3, complete 607-page edition

lem-tdmath-relative-boundary-support.statement: Let $C$ be a nonempty convex set in a finite-dimensional affine Euclidean space $H$ of dimension $k\ge1$, let $\operatorname{aff}C=H$, and put $K=\overline{C}^{\,H}$. If $z\in\partial_H K$ (that is, $z\in K$ and every relative neighborhood of $z$ meets $H\setminus K$), then there is a nonzero linear functional $\ell$ on the translation space of $H$ such that $\ell(q-z)\le0$ for all $q\in C$. If $C\subset\mathbb R^d$ has affine dimension at most $d-2$, then every $z\in C$ has at least two distinct ambient supporting hyperplanes containing $\operatorname{aff}C$.

lem-tdmath-relative-entropy-variational-.title: Relative Entropy Variational, Chain, and Conditioning Rules

references.title: H.-O. Georgii and H. Zessin, Large deviations and the maximum entropy principle for marked point random fields
references.locator: Section 2.3, printed p.184 / PDF p.7, relative entropy, variational identity, and specific entropy
