lem-tdmath-relative-entropy-variational-.statement:
Assume AC. Let $P,Q$ be probability measures on one measurable space and use $D(P\Vert Q)$ as defined in [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]. Then
$$D(P\Vert Q)=\sup_{\phi\in B_b}\left(P(\phi)-\log Q(e^\phi)\right),$$
where $B_b$ is the set of bounded real measurable functions. In particular $D\geq0$. If $T$ is measurable, then $D(P\circ T^{-1}\Vert Q\circ T^{-1})\leq D(P\Vert Q)$.

For standard-Borel spaces $X,Y$, probability reference measures $Q_X,Q_Y$, and a joint probability $P_{XY}\ll Q_X\otimes Q_Y$ with finite $D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)$, let $P_{Y|X=x}$ be the conditional law supplied by [[thm-conditional-density-formula]]. Then
$$D(P_{XY}\Vert Q_X\otimes Q_Y)=D(P_X\Vert Q_X)+\int_X D(P_{Y|X=x}\Vert Q_Y)\,P_X(dx).$$
More generally, for random variables $R,S,Y$ taking values in standard-Borel spaces $\mathcal R,\mathcal S,\mathcal Y$, with $R=r(S)$ for a measurable $r:\mathcal S\to\mathcal R$, and a probability reference $Q_Y$ on $\mathcal Y$, the conditional increments
$$G(R):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|R}\Vert Q_Y)\right],\qquad G(S):=E_P\!\left[D(P_{Y|S}\Vert Q_Y)\right]$$
satisfy $0\leq G(R)\leq G(S)$ whenever $D(P_{S,Y}\Vert P_S\otimes Q_Y)<\infty$.

lem-tdmath-spectator-cancellation.title: Spectator cancellation and signed-order algebra

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, Theorem 2.1 and §II.D

lem-tdmath-spectator-cancellation.statement: Under [[def-tdmath-comparison-and-stability]], for equal-mass compounds $A,B,C$, $A+C\preceq B+C$ if and only if $A\preceq B$. The signed relation of [[def-tdmath-signed-comparison]] is well-defined; on nonnegative equal-mass maps it agrees with $\preceq$, is invariant under adding the same finite-support signed map to both sides, and is transitive and closed under adding two comparisons.

post-td-grand-variational-phase-uniquene.title: Selected grand-variational phase uniqueness
post-td-grand-variational-phase-uniquene.physical_scope: Only a named Borel-measurable stable regularly tempered model and parameter point on the positive-temperature branch or explicitly retained hard-core beta-zero branch for which the corresponding translation-invariant variational minimizer is assumed unique; no universal uniqueness or claim at coexistence.

references.title: Hans-Otto Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction, Probability Theory and Related Fields 99 (1994), 171–195

post-td-grand-variational-phase-uniquene.statement:
Fix the selected stable regularly tempered pair model with Borel-measurable $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, $T>0$, $\beta=(k_{\mathrm B}T)^{-1}$ with the SI conventions of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and activity $z>0$. For the superstable branch, require measurable even pair potentials $\varphi_s,\varphi_r$ with $\varphi=\varphi_s+\varphi_r$, where $\varphi_s$ is stable in joules and $\varphi_r(x)\geq0$ joules for every $x$. Require constants $\epsilon>0$ joules and $r_0>0$ in dimensionless coordinates such that $\varphi_r(x)\geq\epsilon$ whenever $\|x\|_\infty\leq r_0$, where $\|x\|_\infty=\max_j|x_j|$. These are exactly the stable-plus-nonnegative-core conditions of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] for $\widehat\varphi$, after energy conversion; this is an additional model hypothesis, not a consequence of stability alone.

Under the Axiom of Choice, use the global measurable configuration space $\Omega$ of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]], consisting of locally finite simple configurations with sigma-algebra generated by bounded-Borel count maps. For $a\in\mathbb R^d$, let $T_a\omega(A)=\omega(A-a)$ be its measurable translation. A probability law $P$ on $\Omega$ is stationary exactly when $P\circ T_a^{-1}=P$ for every $a\in\mathbb R^d$. For a bounded Borel region $A$, equip its finite simple configuration set $\mathcal C_A$ with $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}=\sigma(N_B:B\subseteq A\text{ Borel})$, without completing it. On this space $r_A(\omega)=\omega\cap A$ is measurable: each generating count satisfies $N_B\circ r_A=N_B$, a bounded-Borel global count. Write $P_A=P\circ r_A^{-1}$ on this exact count sigma-algebra for every stationary $P$. This assertion does not extend $P_A$ to the completed quotient sigma-algebra. The reference $Q_A=Q\circ r_A^{-1}$ is the restriction of the same unit-intensity law $Q$; by [[thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-properties]] and the count-generated restriction sigma-algebra, it equals the restriction to $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$ of the finite-sector law $e^{-|A|}\sum_{N\geq0}\mu_{A,N}$ of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This count sigma-algebra is contained in the completed quotient sigma-algebra: in each sector, the pullback of $N_B$ is $\sum_{j=1}^N\mathbf1_B(x_j)$, a Borel function, so each count generator is quotient measurable. Thus the stated restriction of the positional measure is defined. Relative entropy and the restrictions below always use $\mathcal F_A^{\rm count}$, exactly as in the mathematical global supplier, rather than an unproved completion for arbitrary $P$. Indeed, a finite Borel partition of $A$ has multinomial counts under each fixed-$N$ Lebesgue sector, and summing these sector measures with the factor $e^{-|A|}$ gives independent Poisson counts of the corresponding volumes. Use the finite-region relative entropy $D(P_0\|Q_0)$ of [[def-tdmath-finite-region-relative-entropy]]: if $P_0\ll Q_0$ and $h=dP_0/dQ_0$, then $D=\int h\log h\,dQ_0$ with $0\log0=0$; otherwise $D=+\infty$. Let $C=[-1/2,1/2)^d$ and define $\rho(P)=E_PN_C$. On stationary laws for which the finite limits exist, define
$$I(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{D(P_{\Lambda_L}\|Q_{\Lambda_L})}{|\Lambda_L|},\qquad \Phi(P)=\lim_{L\to\infty}\frac{E_P[H_{\Lambda_L}^{\mathrm{free}}]}{|\Lambda_L|}.$$
For $\beta>0$, use the stationary laws with finite $I(P)$ and $\Phi(P)$ and adopt, at the selected $(\varphi,\beta,z)$, that
$$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{P}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}=\{P^\ast\}.$$

For the $\beta=0$ branch, require a nonempty hard-core displacement set $B=\{x:\varphi(x)=+\infty\}$ and use [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]]. A global configuration is hard-admissible when no pair of its distinct points has displacement in $B$. Restrict to stationary laws assigning probability one to hard-admissible configurations and having finite $I(P)$; adopt, at the selected $z$, that
$$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{P}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}=\{P^\ast\}.$$
These are two explicit parameter-specific physical model restrictions. They do not assert uniqueness for every activity or temperature, do not apply at coexistence when the minimizer set has several elements, and do not infer uniqueness from thermodynamic smoothness.

post-td-simple-system-geometric-axioms.title: Simple-system geometric axioms
post-td-simple-system-geometric-axioms.physical_scope: Adopted convexity, irreversibility, support regularity and boundary-connectivity conditions on the forward sectors of simple thermodynamic state domains and admitted joins.

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, §§III.A–III.B
André Thess, The Lieb–Yngvason Machine: A didactical tool for the definition of entropy in classical thermodynamics, §2
Goddard, The second law of thermodynamics as variation on a theme of Carathéodory, §3

post-td-simple-system-geometric-axioms.statement:
For each simple-system chart $\Gamma_i\subset\mathbb R^{n_i+1}$, $n_i\ge1$, let $x=(u,v)$, with one energy coordinate $u$ and $n_i$ work coordinates $v$. The chart is a nonempty open convex domain. The simple-compressible physical case is the fixed-composition slice and embedding of [[def-td-thermal-join]], with $n_i=1$, $u=U/(1\,\mathrm J)$ and $v=V/(1\,\mathrm{m^3})$. A declared multi-work chart or joined chart instead supplies its own equilibrium endpoint domain and diagonal unit map: $U=u(1\,\mathrm J)$ and $W_a=v_a w_a$ for fixed positive work-coordinate units $w_a$. The numerical domain is identified with these physical endpoints by that supplied map, and accessibility is pulled back from the admitted endpoint relation. These identifications preserve the internal-energy meaning and fixed composition; extra work coordinates do not follow from the simple-compressible state definition. Adopt these assumptions for every state $x$ and for every thermal join treated as a simple system:

**A7 (convex-combination accessibility).** For $0<t<1$, the separated scaled pair $(t x,(1-t)y)$ is accessible to the chart state $t x+(1-t)y$, whenever these states are in the declared domains.

For each $x$, define its forward sector $A_x=\{y\in\Gamma_i:x\prec y\}$. Adopt:

**S1 (strict successor).** Some $y\in\Gamma_i$ satisfies $x\prec\prec y$.

**S2 (unique finite-slope support).** At $x=(u_x,v_x)$, $A_x$ has exactly one supporting hyperplane through $x$, and it can be written
$$
u-u_x+P_i(x)\cdot(v-v_x)=0
$$
with finite $P_i(x)\in\mathbb R^{n_i}$. The map $P_i:\Gamma_i\to\mathbb R^{n_i}$ is locally Lipschitz: every point has a neighborhood on which one finite Lipschitz constant bounds $\|P_i(x)-P_i(y)\|/\|x-y\|$. A supporting hyperplane means $A_x$ lies in one of its closed half-spaces and meets it at $x$.

**S3 (connected relative boundary).** The boundary $\partial_{\Gamma_i}A_x$, taken in the topology relative to $\Gamma_i$, is arcwise connected.

These are explicit adopted conditions. The slope $P_i$ is a geometric support parameter here; no equation identifying it with measured pressure is asserted. In particular, S1–S3 and A7 do not assert comparison hypothesis for products.

pthm-td-clapeyron-local.title: Local Clapeyron slope on a regular pure-phase coexistence branch
pthm-td-clapeyron-local.physical_scope: A one-component, positive-temperature, C1 coexistence branch with bilateral energy, volume, and species exchange, nonzero molar-volume jump, and the explicit local same-tag homogeneity and reversible-heat assumptions stated here, with homogeneity either independently stipulated or supplied on each designated common-law bulk branch through the local Euler theorem; the slope formula requires nonzero molar-volume jump and C1 branch charts and is not asserted when either condition fails.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, author-hosted complete lecture notes, §§4.3.3–4.4 and 5.1.1–5.1.2
David Tong, Statistical Physics, author-hosted complete lecture notes, Chapter 5, §§5.1.1–5.1.3
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Statistical Mechanics, §4.1 First-order phase transitions

pthm-td-clapeyron-local.statement:
Let $\alpha,\beta$ be two one-component phase branches from [[def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain]] on a common open chart $O\subset(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R$ with coordinates $(T,p)$. Assume each branch has a local $C^2$ energy representation $\mathcal U_i(s,V,n)$, $i\in\{\alpha,\beta\}$, and that within each fixed branch tag it satisfies the same-tag homogeneity
$$
\mathcal U_i(\lambda s,\lambda V,\lambda n)=\lambda\mathcal U_i(s,V,n)
$$
for all $\lambda$ in a neighborhood of $1$ for which the scaled state remains in the chart. This is a phase-branch hypothesis: the general tagged law of [[post-td-bulk-additivity]] does not imply it. It may be stipulated independently on each local branch, or supplied by the common-law bulk subclass of [[pthm-td-euler-and-gibbs-duhem]] when each phase's local inverse states lie in its designated entropy cone with fixed species and intensive parameters and common SI units and energy/entropy reference conventions. That supplied subclass uses local inverse uniqueness and does not require a global energy inverse.

Suppose a state $(T_0,p_0)\in O$ is an attained interior coexistence equilibrium with bilateral energy, volume, and species exchange between the two branches, and both branches admit the valid local Gibbs charts of [[def-td-legendre-potentials]]. Write $g_i=G_i/n_i$, $s_i=S_i/n_i$, and $v_i=V_i/n_i$ in the units specified by [[def-td-si-quantities]]. If
$$
\Delta v(T_0,p_0):=v_\beta(T_0,p_0)-v_\alpha(T_0,p_0)\ne0,
$$
then, on some open interval about $T_0$, the equal-Gibbs-per-mole coexistence condition $g_\alpha(T,p(T))=g_\beta(T,p(T))$ defines a unique local $C^1$ curve and
$$
\frac{dp}{dT}=\frac{s_\beta-s_\alpha}{v_\beta-v_\alpha}.
$$
If, in addition, conversion from $\alpha$ to $\beta$ is admitted as a reversible process in contact with an ideal thermal reservoir at the same fixed $T$, and the full finite isolated compound (converted phases, reservoir, work stores and all auxiliaries) has equilibrium endpoints with additive component entropy, with every component other than the converted phases and that reservoir having zero entropy change, then its molar latent heat absorbed by the system is $\ell_{\alpha\to\beta}=T(s_\beta-s_\alpha)$. These are conditional model deductions. The slope conclusion is not asserted when $\Delta v=0$ or where the branch charts are not $C^1$.

pthm-td-controlled-continuum-thermodynam.title: Controlled continuum interval-energy thermodynamic limit
pthm-td-controlled-continuum-thermodynam.physical_scope: Superstable regular classical positional pair systems in periodic cubes at positive temperature, together with the expressly defined formal retained-hard-admissibility zero-inverse-temperature branch, with a nondegenerate density interval and strict upper-energy threshold; periodically continued local convergence requires the stated unique minimizer.

references.title: Hans-Otto Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction, Probability Theory and Related Fields 99 (1994), 171–195
David Tong, Statistical Physics (author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes)
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part SM: Statistical Mechanics (2024 author-hosted lecture notes)

pthm-td-controlled-continuum-thermodynam.statement:
Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB, as required by the current variational-pressure supplier. Let $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, and assume $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable. Require the exact superstable regular hypotheses of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] for this dimensionless potential: a stable part plus a nonnegative core part bounded below by a positive constant on an $\ell^\infty$-ball, with the supplier's lower and upper regular tail conditions. Use $\widehat H=H/E_0$, $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta$ for $\beta>0$, and $\widehat e=e/E_0$; then $\beta H=\widehat\beta\widehat H$. For this supplier convention, let $\nu$ be the supremum of finite-entropy, finite-energy attainable densities for $\widehat\varphi$, and write $\widehat\Phi(P)$ for the supplier's limiting positional energy density; let $e_0(\rho)=\inf\{\widehat\Phi(P):\rho(P)=\rho,\ I(P)<\infty\}$ be its numerical positional-energy infimum. Let $D\subset[0,\infty)$ be a nondegenerate density interval, and require $\inf D<\nu$ and $\widehat e>\inf_{\rho\in D}e_0(\rho)$. Use the supplier's periodic cubes $\Lambda_n$ of numerical volume $V_n=|\Lambda_n|$ and define explicitly
$$A_n=\{\omega:N_{\Lambda_n}(\omega)/V_n\in D,\ H_{n,\mathrm{per}}(\omega)/(E_0V_n)\le\widehat e\},\qquad \widehat e=e/E_0.$$
Here $H_{n,\mathrm{per}}$ is the physical positional energy in joules in the same periodic convention; equivalently its event inequality is $H_{n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n\le e$. For every $n$ with positive event probability, the prepared law is $R_n(B)=Q_{\Lambda_n}(B\cap A_n)/Q_{\Lambda_n}(A_n)$ on the finite count sigma-algebra. Equivalently, with $M_n=\sum_{N\ge0}\mu_{\Lambda_n,N}$, $R_n(B)=M_n(B\cap A_n)/M_n(A_n)$, since $Q_{\Lambda_n}=e^{-V_n}M_n$; use the count-sigma restriction of these positional measures. This defines the density-interval/upper-energy conditional preparation and its conditioned laws. For $\beta>0$, the finite-volume grand and microcanonical weights are those of [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]]. For $\beta=0$, require a nonempty hard-core displacement set and use the formal retained-admissibility continuation of [[def-td-retained-hard-core-zero-beta-preparation]]; do not interpret $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

For both the positive-$\beta$ branch and the formal retained-hard-core $\beta=0$ branch, [[thm-tdmath-interval-event-ensemble-limit]] gives eventual event positivity, the constrained entropy-rate limit, and common-minimizer accumulation points; at $\beta=0$, [[thm-tdmath-retained-hard-zero-beta-limit]] identifies the matching retained grand law and minimizer set. If the relevant common minimizer set is the singleton adopted in [[post-td-grand-variational-phase-uniqueness]] for the multiplier pair supplied by that branch, both the conditioned laws and the corresponding periodic grand laws converge locally to $P^\ast$ for every measurable local observable $f$ with $|f|\leq c(1+N_A)$ on a bounded region $A$. This is an interval-density and upper-energy result, not a fixed-particle-number or shrinking-shell theorem.


Here local observables are evaluated on the periodic continuation of the prepared torus configuration. This is the same periodic boundary preparation, with no new physical sampling assumption; a configuration is not extended by the empty configuration outside its fundamental cube.

pthm-td-controlled-thermodynamic-ensembl.title: Controlled canonical–grand thermodynamic duality
pthm-td-controlled-thermodynamic-ensembl.physical_scope: Stable regularly tempered classical positional Borel pair models at positive temperature, for the closed concave extension of the attainable canonical rate; no local-observable equivalence is asserted.

references.title: Hans-Otto Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction, Probability Theory and Related Fields 99 (1994), 171–195
David Tong, Statistical Physics (author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes)
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part SM: Statistical Mechanics (2024 author-hosted lecture notes)

pthm-td-controlled-thermodynamic-ensembl.statement:
Assume AC and $T>0$, with $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$. Under the stable regularly tempered positional model of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]] and the adopted ensemble weights of [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]], assume the dimensionless potential $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$ is Borel measurable as required by the current mathematical carriers. Set $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$ and $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta$; write $F(\rho,\beta)$ and $P(\alpha,\beta)$ for the mathematical rates evaluated at $\widehat\beta$. Let $F(\rho,\beta)$ be the canonical log-partition rate per dimensionless reference volume, defined on interior attainable densities by the fixed-density limit and extended to the closed effective density domain by the upper-semicontinuous concave extension specified in [[thm-tdmath-canonical-grand-duality]]. Let
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\lim_{V\to\infty}V^{-1}\log\sum_{N\geq0}e^{\alpha N}Z(V,N),\qquad \alpha=\log z.$$
Then
$$P(\alpha,\beta)=\sup_{\rho\geq0}\{F(\rho,\beta)+\alpha\rho\},\qquad F(\rho,\beta)=\inf_{\alpha\in\mathbb R}\{P(\alpha,\beta)-\alpha\rho\}.$$
In physical units, $p=(k_BT/\ell_0^d)P$ and the positional Helmholtz free-energy density is $f_{\mathrm{pos}}=-(k_BT/\ell_0^d)F$, with the fixed reference normalization of [[post-td-classical-indistinguishable-particle-measure]]. This duality concerns limiting thermodynamic functions only. It does not imply local ensemble equivalence, uniqueness of a phase, or convergence at excluded density endpoints.

pthm-td-entropy-under-product-comparison.title: Entropy representation for finite separated products
pthm-td-entropy-under-product-comparison.physical_scope: An order representation for the declared finite family of simple systems under the adopted contact assumptions; the entropy is dimensionless until an independent physical calibration fixes its unit.

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, Theorems 2.2 and 4.8 and §IV.B
André Thess, The Lieb–Yngvason Machine: A didactical tool for the definition of entropy in classical thermodynamics, §§2–4
Goddard, The second law of thermodynamics as variation on a theme of Carathéodory, §§2–3

pthm-td-entropy-under-product-comparison.statement:
Let $I$ be a nonempty, possibly infinite set of primitive system labels. Assume the declared family includes every finite separated product and every finite thermal join, and that every finite join-closed subfamily satisfies the hypotheses of [[pthm-td-contact-product-comparison]]. Also assume the explicit finite-factor representation of [[def-td-scaled-products-and-comparison]] and the Axiom of Choice. Then there is a single dimensionless function $\widetilde S$ on all states of the declared finite-factor family that is additive under separation, extensive under every admitted positive scaling, and characterizes every equal-composition comparison:

$$ A\prec B\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \widetilde S(A)\le \widetilde S(B). $$

For each simple chart, A7 also makes $\widetilde S$ concave on every convex region where the stated recombination operation is admitted. The result does not set the entropy unit to $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$, determine additive constants across different reaction compositions, or establish empirical validity of the contact assumptions.

pthm-td-interacting-three-ensemble-local.title: Interacting exact-N shrinking-shell three-ensemble local limit
pthm-td-interacting-three-ensemble-local.physical_scope: Superstable regular classical positional Borel pair systems in periodic boxes, at positive temperature and interior density, with differentiable canonical rate and a singleton grand variational minimizer; local observables use the same periodic continuation, and kinetic momentum is excluded.

references.title: Hans-Otto Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction, Probability Theory and Related Fields 99 (1994), 171–195
David Tong, Statistical Physics (author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes)
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part SM: Statistical Mechanics (2024 author-hosted lecture notes)

pthm-td-interacting-three-ensemble-local.statement:
Assume AC, the ultrafilter extension principle, DC, and HB as required by the current variational-pressure supplier. Let $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, and assume $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable. Require the exact superstable regular hypotheses of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]; use $\widehat H=H/E_0$ and $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta>0$ in its mathematical suppliers. Let $F(\rho,\beta)$ denote the numerical canonical rate evaluated at $\widehat\beta$; assume it is differentiable in physical $\beta$ at the chosen temperature and set $e=-\partial_\beta F(\rho,\beta)$, in joules per dimensionless reference volume. For periodic cubes $\Lambda_n$, take exact particle numbers $N_n$ with $N_n/V_n\to\rho$ at a positive interior attainable density. Choose a finite supporting activity parameter $\alpha$ for $F$ at $\rho$ and set $z=e^\alpha>0$; assume the corresponding stationary grand variational minimizer is the singleton $P^\ast$ as in [[post-td-grand-variational-phase-uniqueness]].

Then there exists a constructed sequence $\delta_n\downarrow0$ for which the periodic exact-$N_n$ canonical positional law, the periodic grand-canonical law at $(\alpha,\beta)$, and the uniform positional shell law of [[def-td-controlled-fixed-n-energy-shell]] on
$$N=N_n,\qquad |H_{L_n,\mathrm{per}}/V_n-e|\leq\delta_n,\qquad L_n=2n+1$$
all converge locally to $P^\ast$. Convergence means convergence of expectations for every measurable local observable $f$ supported in a bounded region and satisfying $|f|\leq c(1+N_A)$ there. The shell sequence is constructed from canonical concentration; arbitrary preassigned shrinking widths, exact zero-width surfaces, full phase-space shells involving kinetic momentum, and a conclusion at nonunique minimizers are not asserted.

Here local observables are evaluated on the periodic continuation of the prepared torus configuration. This is the same periodic boundary preparation, with no new physical sampling assumption; a configuration is not extended by the empty configuration outside its fundamental cube.

pthm-td-qualified-van-hove-and-exterior-.title: Qualified van Hove and tempered-exterior thermodynamic limits
pthm-td-qualified-van-hove-and-exterior-.physical_scope: Classical positional Borel pair systems in dimension at least two; van Hove free-wall limits require superstability and regularity, while deterministic exterior limits additionally require a genuine positive divergent core in the supplier's infinity norm and a fixed uniformly tempered exterior class.

references.title: Hans-Otto Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction, Probability Theory and Related Fields 99 (1994), 171–195
David Ruelle, Superstable Interactions in Classical Statistical Mechanics, Communications in Mathematical Physics 18 (1970), 127–159
David Tong, Statistical Physics (author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes)
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part SM: Statistical Mechanics (2024 author-hosted lecture notes)

pthm-td-qualified-van-hove-and-exterior-.statement:
Assume AC, as required by the current mathematical definition and its shape suppliers. Let $d\geq2$, $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$, and assume $\widehat\varphi$ is Borel measurable and superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. Use $\widehat H=H/E_0$ and $\widehat\beta=E_0(k_BT)^{-1}>0$ in the mathematical rates. Let $(\Lambda_k)$ be a van Hove sequence as in [[def-td-admissible-van-hove-and-tempered-exterior]]. First, for free walls, the positional grand pressure along $\Lambda_k$ converges to the free-cube pressure of [[pthm-td-stable-tempered-free-cube-grand-pressure]]. For any positive interior attainable density $\rho$ and exact integers $N_k$ with $N_k/|\Lambda_k|\to\rho$, the exact-$N_k$ free-wall canonical log-partition rate converges to the same cube canonical rate. These two shape statements require superstability and regularity; stability alone is not asserted to suffice for arbitrary van Hove shapes.

Second, strengthen the potential hypothesis: for some $r_0>0$, $\widehat\varphi(x)\geq\widehat\chi(\|x\|_\infty)>0$ whenever $0<\|x\|_\infty\leq r_0$, where $\widehat\chi$ is nonincreasing and $\int_0^{r_0}\widehat\chi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr=+\infty$. For each fixed $t<\infty$, the free-wall grand pressure in $\Lambda_n$ with exterior $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$ then converges uniformly in $\zeta$ to the same free-cube pressure. The exterior interaction is the deterministic positional term of [[def-td-admissible-van-hove-and-tempered-exterior]], not a volume-filling external field. This genuine divergent-core condition is the exact stronger hypothesis of the current exterior supplier; it is not inferred from superstability or replaced by a weaker source condition.

pthm-td-regular-gibbs-phase-rule.title: Local regular dimension of a reacting Gibbs phase-coexistence manifold
pthm-td-regular-gibbs-phase-rule.physical_scope: Interior compositions of finitely many C1 intensive phase branches with energy, volume, all listed species exchanges, and internal reactions allowed in every phase, at a solution where the combined coexistence-and-affinity Jacobian has a nonsingular minor; phase amounts and externally fixed variables are excluded, and the conclusion is not asserted where a C1 phase chart fails, composition lies on the simplex boundary, or the nonsingular-minor hypothesis fails.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, author-hosted complete lecture notes, §5.1.1
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics: Statistical Mechanics, §4.1 First-order phase transitions

pthm-td-regular-gibbs-phase-rule.statement:
Assume the entropy of each phase is $C^2$ on its physical state chart and its derivative-defined temperature at the endpoint is finite and positive. The equation-set dimension below concerns this smooth interior state only.

Let $C\ge1$ be the number of named species, $P\ge1$ the number of coexisting phase branches, and $R\ge0$ the number of independent internal reaction directions. Consider an attained global entropy-maximizing endpoint on the exact feasible set of [[def-td-isolated-compound-feasible-set]]. For each phase $\alpha$, use an intensive phase branch from [[def-td-phase-and-coexistence-domain]] and an interior composition $x^\alpha\in\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ}$. Let each branch chemical-potential map
$$
\mu^\alpha(T,p,x^\alpha)=(\mu_1^\alpha,\ldots,\mu_C^\alpha)
$$
be $C^1$ on a common open domain
$$
\mathcal U=(0,\infty)\times\mathbb R\times(\Delta_{C-1}^{\circ})^P \subseteq\mathbb R^{\,n},\qquad n=2+P(C-1).
$$
Assume energy, volume, and every named species can be exchanged between every phase pair in both directions, and every listed reaction direction is feasible in both extent directions in every phase while that phase's energy, volume, other reaction extents, and all other phase coordinates are held fixed at the coexistence point. Let $\nu^1,\ldots,\nu^R\in\mathbb R^C$ be linearly independent, dimensionless stoichiometric vectors, with extents measured in moles. Phase equilibrium imposes $\mu_i^\alpha-\mu_i^1=0$ for $1\le i\le C$, $2\le\alpha\le P$; internal reaction equilibrium imposes $(\nu^r)^{\mathsf T}\mu^\alpha=0$ in every phase for $1\le r\le R$. On the phase-equality locus these are the same $R$ equations in each phase, so count them once using phase 1. Put $q:=C(P-1)$ and $m:=q+R$. If $m=0$ (equivalently $P=1,R=0$), no equation is imposed and the local zero set is the whole chart, of dimension $n=C+1=C-P+2-R$. If $m\ge1$ and the combined equation map has an invertible $m\times m$ derivative minor at the solution, with $m\le n$, then the local zero set of these first-order coexistence-and-affinity equations is a graph of dimension
$$
n-q-R=C-P+2-R.
$$
This is the dimension of the equation zero set in intensive coordinates only; phase amounts and their extensive conservation constraints are not counted, and the actual stable-coexistence set may be a proper subset after additional stability constraints. If the nonsingular-minor condition fails, no dimension formula is asserted.

pthm-td-stable-tempered-free-cube-grand-.title: Stable-tempered free-cube grand pressure
pthm-td-stable-tempered-free-cube-grand-.physical_scope: Positive-temperature grand-canonical positional preparations in cubic free-wall boxes for stable even Borel pair potentials with the explicitly stated decreasing integrable tail.

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics (author-hosted Cambridge lecture notes)
Konstantin K. Likharev, Essential Graduate Physics, Part SM: Statistical Mechanics (2024 author-hosted lecture notes)
Hans-Otto Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction, Probability Theory and Related Fields 99 (1994), 171–195

pthm-td-stable-tempered-free-cube-grand-.statement:
Assume AC. Let $d\geq2$, $\varphi$ be stable with the regular integrable tail of [[def-td-stable-tempered-continuum-preparation]], and assume its dimensionless representative $\widehat\varphi=\varphi/E_0$ is Borel measurable, as required by the current mathematical supplier. Take $E_0=1\,\mathrm J$, $\beta=(k_BT)^{-1}$, and $\widehat\beta=E_0\beta>0$. For cubes $\Lambda_L=[-L/2,L/2)^d$, let $\Xi_L(z,\beta)$ be the free-wall grand partition function specified by [[post-td-equilibrium-ensemble-sampling]]. Then the positional grand pressure
$$p_L(z,T)=\frac{k_BT}{\ell_0^d|\Lambda_L|}\log\Xi_L(z,\beta)$$
has a finite limit as $L\to\infty$. In the dimensionless reference-volume convention of [[thm-tdmath-canonical-grand-duality]], let $P(\alpha,\widehat\beta)=\lim_{L\to\infty}|\Lambda_L|^{-1}\log\Xi_L(e^\alpha,\widehat\beta)$, where the supplier uses numerical energies in units of $E_0$. Then $p=(k_BT/\ell_0^d)P(\log z,\widehat\beta)$. This is a conditional model deduction, not a measurement or an assertion that every real gas realizes the preparation.

rem-td-nonsmooth-phase-scope.title: Scope at phase boundaries and in the thermodynamic limit
rem-td-nonsmooth-phase-scope.physical_scope: Interpretive limits for the phase-branch, coexistence, Clapeyron, and compact-mixture statements on this page; this remark establishes no universal critical or thermodynamic-limit result.

rem-td-nonsmooth-phase-scope.statement:
The branch theorems on this page require the stated smooth local charts. Here coexistence means equality of the declared intensive phase data at an admitted endpoint; it does not itself imply loss of chart regularity. The smooth-branch conclusions apply only on their specified C1 charts and interior composition domains. They supply no conclusion where a branch chart fails to be C1, a species amount reaches the composition boundary, or the specified coexistence-and-affinity Jacobian lacks its required nonsingular minor. In particular, [[pthm-td-clapeyron-local]] requires a nonzero molar-volume jump; when that jump vanishes, its local graph argument and quotient formula do not apply.

The compact-mixture result [[pthm-td-compact-continuous-phase-mixture]] requires a compact phase-generator domain, a continuous entropy map, a fixed barycenter, and feasibility of all probability mixtures with that barycenter. It supplies no attainment theorem for noncompact domains. Likewise, [[def-td-thermodynamic-limit-contract]] specifies the sequence and normalization for a limiting claim but proves no limit exists and no derivatives commute with that limit.

A finite-state partition sum is finite and positive at each finite system size. A singular phase behavior therefore needs a separately specified limit or another model with a separately established domain and regularity analysis. This page does not assert a universal thermodynamic-limit theorem, ensemble equivalence, critical exponent, or physical applicability of the van der Waals equation.

The local homogeneity used by [[pthm-td-clapeyron-local]] may be independently stipulated in a phase model or supplied on the separately designated common-law bulk branch under the local Euler theorem's inverse-chart and common-reference conditions. A constructed local Gibbs model need not be embedded in a global bulk cone to use the general conditional result. The added branch supplies no universal finite-size, long-range or gravitational extensivity and does not remove any smoothness, exchange or nonzero-volume-jump condition.

thm-tdmath-discrete-quantum-cesaro-depha.title: Trace-norm Cesàro dephasing for a discrete Gibbs spectrum

references.title: Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics
references.locator: Complete 635-page lecture notes retrieved and read; §§4.2–4.6, pp.192–217, ensembles, microcanonical phase space, quantum density matrices, and traces.

thm-tdmath-discrete-quantum-cesaro-depha.statement:
Assume the Axiom of Choice and the exact first-clause interface of [[thm-tdmath-general-trace-gibbs-model]]: a nonzero complex Hilbert space has a finite or countable complete orthonormal energy eigenbasis $(u_j)$ for a self-adjoint semibounded $A$, with each energy eigenspace finite-dimensional. The supplier is a current draft whose statement and complete argument have been inspected; this theorem is conditional on that interface and does not claim its independent acceptance. Let $\hbar>0$, define $U_tu_j=e^{-iE_jt/\hbar}u_j$, and extend linearly and continuously. For any positive trace-class density operator $\rho$ with $\operatorname{Tr}\rho=1$, set $\rho_t=U_t\rho U_t^*$. If $P_E$ denotes the projection onto the full eigenspace of energy $E$, then the trace-norm Riemann average
$$\bar\rho_T:=\frac1T\int_0^T\rho_t\,dt$$
converges as $T\to\infty$ to
$$\rho_{\rm diag}:=\sum_E P_E\rho P_E$$
in trace norm. The full degenerate energy blocks are retained. Thus expectations of every bounded observable converge to their diagonal-ensemble values. This asserts Cesàro convergence, not convergence of $\rho_t$ at individual late times, and is restricted to the stated discrete trace-class spectrum.

thm-tdmath-dominated-convergence.statement: Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $f_n:X\to\mathbb C$ be measurable with $f_n\to f$ almost everywhere. Suppose $g\ge0$ is measurable and $\int g\,d\mu<\infty$, and $|f_n|\le g$ almost everywhere for every $n$. Let $f_0(x)$ be the finite complex pointwise limit of $(f_n(x))$ where it exists, and $0$ elsewhere. Then $f_0$ is measurable, equals $f$ almost everywhere, is integrable, and $\int f_n\,d\mu\to\int f_0\,d\mu$ and $\int|f_n-f_0|\,d\mu\to0$. If the specified $f$ is measurable, these same conclusions hold with $f$ in place of $f_0$. In particular this is automatic when $\mu$ is complete. On a noncomplete measure space an arbitrary almost-everywhere representative need not be measurable, so no integral of such a nonmeasurable $f$ is asserted.

thm-tdmath-finite-mixture-envelope.title: Finite-mixture convex envelope and its supporting-face condition

references.title: R. T. Rockafellar, Convex Analysis, §§12, 18, and 23
P. Bianchi, O. Fercoq, and W. Hachem, Elements of Convex Analysis and Optimization, §§1.1–1.5 and 2.1–2.3
Zhiyuan Li, Lecture 4: Convex Conjugates and Marginal Duality

thm-tdmath-finite-mixture-envelope.statement:
Let $m\ge1$, let $q_1,\ldots,q_m\in\mathbb R^d$, and let $a_1,\ldots,a_m\in\mathbb R$. Put

$$\Delta_m=\{\theta\in\mathbb R^m:\theta_i\ge0,\ \sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i=1\},\qquad P:=\left\{\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_iq_i:\theta\in\Delta_m\right\}.$$

Thus $P$ is the finite convex hull of the listed points, defined here as their convex combinations.

For $x\in P$ let $\Theta_x=\{\theta\in\Delta_m:\sum_i\theta_iq_i=x\}$ and define

$$f_{\rm mix}(x)=\min_{\theta\in\Theta_x}\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i a_i;$$

set $f_{\rm mix}(x)=+\infty$ for $x\notin P$. Then every minimum is attained; $f_{\rm mix}$ is proper, lower semicontinuous, and convex; and it is pointwise greatest among convex functions $h:\mathbb R^d\to\overline{\mathbb R}$ satisfying $h(q_i)\le a_i$ for every $i$. Consequently $f_{\rm mix}=f_{\rm mix}^{**}$. If $p\in\partial f_{\rm mix}(x)$ and $\theta$ is any minimizing mixture for $x$, then every $i$ with $\theta_i>0$ satisfies

$$a_i=\langle p,q_i\rangle-f_{\rm mix}^*(p).$$

Thus all occupied data points $(q_i,a_i)$ lie on one supporting affine hyperplane. The assertion is finite-dimensional and makes no claim about infinite families.

Then $\widetilde p_L$ has the same limit. The result covers finite-alphabet, bounded, translation-invariant finite-range interactions on cubic boxes; it asserts no continuum-particle or long-range limit.

thm-tdmath-forward-boundary-graph.statement:
Under [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], each simple domain has one orientation sign $\varepsilon_i\in\{-1,1\}$, constant across the domain, such that at fixed work coordinate $v$, $x\prec y$ exactly when $\varepsilon_i(u_y-u_x)\ge0$. In coordinates oriented so $\varepsilon_i=1$, for each $x\in\Gamma_i$ the projection $\rho_x$ of $\partial_{\Gamma_i}A_x$ onto work coordinates is open and connected; the boundary is the graph $(u_x(v),v)$ of a $C^1$ function with locally Lipschitz derivative

$$Du_x(v)=-P_i(u_x(v),v).$$

If $y\in\partial A_x$, then $A_y=A_x$ and their boundary graphs agree.

thm-tdmath-grand-response-covariance.statement: Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $w:X\to[0,\infty)$ and $X_a:X\to\mathbb R$ ($1\le a\le r$) be measurable, and let $U\subseteq\mathbb R^r$ be open. For $\theta=(\theta_1,\ldots,\theta_r)$, define $\theta\cdot X(x):=\sum_{a=1}^r\theta_aX_a(x)$. Set $Z(\theta):=\int w\exp(\theta\cdot X)\,d\mu$ and assume $0<Z(\theta)<\infty$ on $U$. Suppose for every compact $K\subset U$ there is an integrable $G_K\ge0$ such that $w e^{\theta\cdot X}(1+\sum_a|X_a|^2)\le G_K$ pointwise for all $\theta\in K$. For the normalized density $p_\theta=w e^{\theta\cdot X}/Z(\theta)$, define $\mathbb E_\theta Y:=\int Yp_\theta\,d\mu$ when integrable and $\operatorname{Cov}_\theta(X_a,X_b):=\mathbb E_\theta[(X_a-\mathbb E_\theta X_a)(X_b-\mathbb E_\theta X_b)]$. Then $\partial_a\log Z=\mathbb E_\theta X_a$ and $\partial_b\mathbb E_\theta X_a=\operatorname{Cov}_\theta(X_a,X_b)$. Thus the Hessian of $\log Z$ is positive semidefinite. This is a mathematical model identity; it assumes no independence or absence of correlations.

thm-tdmath-independent-microcanonical-bl.title: Finite-site microcanonical and canonical block equivalence

references.title: David Tong, Statistical Physics, complete author-hosted lecture text

thm-tdmath-independent-microcanonical-bl.statement:
Let $A=\{1,\ldots,q\}$, $q\ge1$, have real energies $e_j$, and fix finite $\beta\in\mathbb R$. Set $Z_1=\sum_j e^{-\beta e_j}$, $p_j=e^{-\beta e_j}/Z_1>0$, and $E=\sum_jp_je_j$. For each $N\ge1$, let $\delta_N\ge q\sum_{j=1}^q|e_j|$ and $\delta_N/N\to0$. Define the shell $\Gamma_N=\{i\in A^N:|\sum_{r=1}^Ne_{i_r}-NE|\le\delta_N\}$ and the uniform law on that shell. For probability laws $\mu,\nu$ on the finite set $A^k$, total variation distance means $\frac12\sum_{x\in A^k}|\mu(x)-\nu(x)|$. Then $\Gamma_N$ is nonempty for every $N$; for each fixed $k\ge1$, the first $k$-site marginal (for $N\ge k$) converges in that distance to $p^{\otimes k}$; and
$$\frac1N\log|\Gamma_N|\longrightarrow H(p):=-\sum_{j=1}^qp_j\log p_j.$$
The conclusion is for this finite alphabet, additive energy, exact shell width and uniform shell law. It does not assert finite-size equality or equivalence for interacting or continuous models.

thm-tdmath-interval-event-ensemble-limit.title: Interacting density-interval and upper-energy event limit

references.title: H.-O. Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction
references.locator: Theorem 4 and Sections 5–7, printed pp.177–195 / PDF pp.7–25: density interval with upper energy event, entropy minimizers and finite multiplier.

thm-tdmath-interval-event-ensemble-limit.statement:
Assume the superstable regular model and Poisson conventions of [[thm-tdmath-continuum-variational-pressure]], with stationary finite-intensity law space $\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}$, intensity $\rho$, specific entropy $I$, and energy density $\Phi$ as there defined. Let $D\subset[0,\infty)$ be an interval of positive length and define
$$\nu=\sup\{\rho(P):P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat},\ I(P)<\infty,\ \Phi(P)<\infty\},\qquad e_0(\rho)=\inf\{\Phi(P):P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat},\ \rho(P)=\rho,\ I(P)<\infty\},$$
with the supremum of an empty set equal to $0$ and the infimum of an empty set equal to $+\infty$. If $\inf D<\nu$ and $e>\inf_{\rho\in D}e_0(\rho)$, define
$$A_L=\{N_{\Lambda_L}/L^d\in D,\ H_{L,\mathrm{per}}/L^d\leq e\}.$$
Then $A_L$ has positive Poisson probability for all sufficiently large $L$, and
$$\lim_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log Q_{\Lambda_L}(A_L) =-\min\{I(P):\rho(P)\in\overline D,\ \Phi(P)\leq e\}.$$
Let $R_{L,\omega}$ be the periodized empirical field of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]], and let $B=\{x\in\mathbb R^d:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$. Define
$$\mathcal K_B=\left\{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}:P\!\left(\left\{\omega:\forall x,y\in\omega,\ x\neq y\Rightarrow x-y\notin B\right\}\right)=1\right\}.$$
For $\beta>0$ put $\mathcal M_{\beta,z}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}$; at $\beta=0$ put $\mathcal M_{0,z}=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal K_B}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}$. Then there are $\beta\geq0$ and $z>0$ for which the empirical fields under the conditional law $Q_{\Lambda_L}(\cdot\mid A_L)$ and the matching periodic grand-canonical law concentrate in every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood of $\mathcal M_{\beta,z}$. If this minimizer set is a singleton, both empirical fields converge to it in probability in $\tau_L$. These are empirical-field conclusions. The periodically continued conditional and grand laws also converge in $\tau_L$ under the same uniqueness assumption, for all measurable local observables of at-most-linear count growth. The energy constraint is an upper event and $D$ is nondegenerate; this does not assert exact $N$, a shrinking shell, or a singular energy surface.
In the $\beta=0$ branch the finite periodic weight is explicitly $z^N$ times the indicator that no displacement between the configuration and any periodic image lies in $B$; no value is assigned to $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

thm-tdmath-measurable-canonical-identiti.statement: Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space, let $E:X\to\mathbb R$ be measurable, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. Suppose $Z(\beta):=\int e^{-\beta E}\,d\mu$ satisfies $0<Z(\beta)<\infty$ on $J$, and for every compact interval $K\subset J$ there is $G_K\in L^1(\mu)$ with $(1+|E|^2)e^{-\beta E}\le G_K$ pointwise for every $\beta\in K$. Define $p_\beta=e^{-\beta E}/Z(\beta)$, $\langle Y\rangle_\beta:=\int Yp_\beta\,d\mu$ for integrable $Y$, and $\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E):=\int(E-\langle E\rangle_\beta)^2p_\beta\,d\mu$. Then $Z\in C^2(J)$, $Z'=-\int E e^{-\beta E}d\mu$, $Z''=\int E^2e^{-\beta E}d\mu$, and $-\partial_\beta\log Z=\langle E\rangle_\beta$, $\partial_\beta^2\log Z=\operatorname{Var}_\beta(E)$. The reference-relative entropy $-\int p_\beta\log p_\beta\,d\mu$ is finite and equals $\log Z+\beta\langle E\rangle_\beta$.

thm-tdmath-monotone-convergence.statement: Let $(X,\Sigma,\mu)$ be a measure space and let $f_n:X\to[0,\infty]$ be measurable with $f_n\le f_{n+1}$ and $f_n\to f$ pointwise. Then $\int f_n\,d\mu\uparrow\int f\,d\mu$, including infinite values. Also, for measurable $f,g\ge0$, $\int(f+g)\,d\mu=\int f\,d\mu+\int g\,d\mu$. For every $c\ge0$, $\int cf\,d\mu=c\int f\,d\mu$; the integral is also linear on real integrable functions.

thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-prope.title: Poisson Reference Counts and Translation Invariance

references.title: H.-O. Georgii and H. Zessin, Large deviations and the maximum entropy principle for marked point random fields
references.locator: Section 2.3, printed p.184 / PDF p.7, Poisson process characterized by independent Poisson counts on disjoint bounded sets

thm-tdmath-poisson-reference-count-prope.statement:
Assume AC, fix $d\geq1$ and $\lambda>0$, and let $Q_\lambda$ be the configuration law of [[def-tdmath-poisson-configuration-reference]]. Define the intensity measure on Borel sets by $\Lambda_{Q_\lambda}(A):=E_{Q_\lambda}N_A$, where $N_A=\omega(A)$ and the nonnegative expectation may be infinite. For pairwise disjoint bounded Borel sets $A_1,\ldots,A_r\subseteq\mathbb R^d$, the restrictions $\omega|_{A_1},\ldots,\omega|_{A_r}$ are independent, each count $N_{A_j}$ has Poisson law with mean $\lambda|A_j|$, and the joint law of counts on any finite disjoint family is the product of those Poisson laws. In particular, $Q_\lambda$ is invariant under every translation $T_x$, and $\Lambda_{Q_\lambda}(A)=\lambda|A|$ for every Borel $A$. For every bounded Borel $A$ and real $a$, its count also has the exact exponential moment
$$E_{Q_\lambda}e^{aN_A}=\exp\!\left(\lambda|A|(e^a-1)\right).$$

thm-tdmath-reference-strip-gluing.title: Reference-strip gluing proves comparison for scaled copies

thm-tdmath-reference-strip-gluing.statement: Assume [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]] and T1–T4 of [[def-tdmath-thermal-contact-hypotheses]] for every finite join. For any one simple type $\Gamma_i$, every two finite compounds of its scaled copies with the same total coefficient mass are comparable. Thus CH holds on all multiple scaled products of that type. thm-tdmath-regular-collision-entropy.title: Conditional Boltzmann entropy inequality and equality form

references.title: David Tong, Kinetic Theory, Part 2

thm-tdmath-regular-collision-entropy.statement:
Let $\Omega=\mathbb T^d$ be a spatial rectangle with opposite faces identified, $d\ge2$, and let $I$ be an open time interval. Suppose $f:\Omega\times\mathbb R^d\times I\to(0,\infty)$ is $C^1$ in space and time and $C^2$ in velocity. Fix a positive reference density $f_{\rm ref}$ with the same units as $f$. Assume $f$, $f|v|^2$, and $f|\log(f/f_{\rm ref})|$ are integrable, and assume an integrable envelope on every compact time interval justifying differentiation of the entropy integral and every displayed collision integral. Let $Q$ and the symmetric collision measure $\nu$ satisfy the weak identity in [[def-tdmath-elastic-collision-kernel]] for tests $1$ and $\log(f/f_{\rm ref})$, with absolute convergence, and suppose
$$\partial_t f+v\cdot\nabla_r f=Q(f).$$
Then for $H[f](t)=\int_\Omega\int_{\mathbb R^d}f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,dv\,dr$,
$$\frac{d}{dt}H[f](t)=-\frac14\int_\Omega\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(A-B)(\log A-\log B)\,d\nu\,dr\le0,\qquad A=f(r,v,t)f(r,w,t),\quad B=f(r,v',t)f(r,w',t).$$
The integrand is nonnegative because $\log$ is strictly increasing. Equality in the entropy-production integral holds exactly when $A=B$ for $\nu$-almost every collision at almost every $r$. Under the additional assumptions that $\nu$ is locally finite, has full support on $Q_{\rm el}$, and $f$ is positive and $C^2$ in $v$, this balance implies for almost every $r$ that
$$\log(f(r,v,t)/f_{\rm ref})=\alpha(r,t)+b(r,t)\cdot v+\frac{\lambda(r,t)}2|v|^2.$$
If $f(r,\cdot,t)$ is integrable over $\mathbb R^d$, then $\lambda(r,t)<0$, so its velocity profile is Maxwellian. Conversely, every profile of this form has zero collision entropy production. The weak collision identity is an explicit model hypothesis; this is not a derivation from reversible many-particle mechanics or a PDE existence theorem.

thm-tdmath-regular-energy-shell-measure.title: Coarea and invariant measure on compact regular energy shells

thm-tdmath-regular-energy-shell-measure.statement:
Assume AC. Let $O\subset\mathbb R^{2n}$ be open with its canonical symplectic form, let $H\in C^2(O,\mathbb R)$, and let $J\subset\mathbb R$ be open. Suppose $\nabla H\ne0$ on $H^{-1}(J)$ and $H^{-1}(K)$ is compact in $O$ for every compact $K\subset J$. Define $\mu_E$ by [[def-tdmath-regular-energy-shell]]. Then for every nonnegative Borel $f$ compactly supported in $H^{-1}(J)$,
$$\int_Of(x)\,dx=\int_J\mu_E(f)\,dE.$$
For every $E\in J$ with nonempty shell $\Sigma_E=H^{-1}(\{E\})$, $0<\mu_E(1)<\infty$, and $\widehat\mu_E=\mu_E/\mu_E(1)$ is a probability measure. Let $\phi_t$ be a Hamiltonian flow map defined as a diffeomorphism on a full compact energy band containing $\Sigma_E$ and preserving that band. Then $\widehat\mu_E$ is invariant under $\phi_t$ for every such regular $E$. Critical levels and noncompact bands are outside this statement.

thm-tdmath-retained-hard-zero-beta-limit.statement:
Let $\phi$ be superstable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], and let $B=\{x:\phi(x)=+\infty\}$. For a finite configuration $\omega$, call it admissible when no pair displacement belongs to $B$; for periodic boxes require this also for every periodic image pair. Define the zero-inverse-temperature-parameter continuation (the mathematical $\beta=0$ branch) to be $z^{N(\omega)}\mathbf 1_{\rm admissible}(\omega)$, explicitly retaining the hard exclusion. Then the normalized Poisson free and periodic partition rates exist and equal
$$-\min_{P\in\mathcal K_B}\{I(P)-\rho(P)\log z\},$$
where $\mathcal K_B$ is the set of stationary laws with no forbidden pair almost surely. The minimizer set is nonempty and compact in $\tau_L$. The periodically continued grand laws are relatively compact in $\tau_L$, all their accumulation points are minimizers, and if this minimizer is unique they converge to it for every measurable local observable of at-most-linear count growth. If $B=\varnothing$, this is the Poisson activity-$z$ model. For $B\ne\varnothing$, it is not an unrestricted Poisson law and does not assign a value to the undefined product $0\cdot(+\infty)$.

thm-tdmath-unattained-cost-entropy-infer.title: Catalyst-chain cost characterizes cross-type transitions

references.title: Lieb and Yngvason, The Physics and Mathematics of the Second Law of Thermodynamics, Theorem 6.1 and proof, pp. 75–76
Daniel Arovas, Lecture Notes on Thermodynamics and Statistical Mechanics, Chapters 2 and 4, complete 607-page edition

thm-tdmath-unattained-cost-entropy-infer.statement:
Assume the calibrated entropy family of [[thm-tdmath-arbitrary-family-calibration]], the cross-type accessibility axioms A1–A6 of [[def-tdmath-forward-sector-hypotheses]], and the decorated cost $F$ of [[def-tdmath-decorated-chain-costs]]. For every pair of types $\Gamma,\Gamma'$ and states $x\in X_\Gamma$, $y\in X_{\Gamma'}$,

$$x\prec y\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \sigma_\Gamma(x)+F(\Gamma,\Gamma')\le \sigma_{\Gamma'}(y).$$

The infimum defining $F$ need not be attained. If $F=+\infty$, the right side is false; if $F=-\infty$, the right side is true.

lem-tdmath-diagonal-model-hilbert-and-do.statement: For the finite or explicitly enumerated countable index set $I$ of [[def-tdmath-diagonal-operator-model]], the inner-product space $\ell^2(I)$ is complete and therefore a complex Hilbert space, with inner product linear in the first variable. For any real family $(E_i)$, the displayed domain $D(H_E)$ is a linear subspace containing every finite-support vector, is dense in $\ell^2(I)$, and $x\mapsto(E_ix_i)_i$ is a linear map from that domain into $\ell^2(I)$. These assertions also hold for the empty finite index set.

thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-li.title: Canonical free-cube limit at every interior attainable density

thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-li.statement:
Let $\phi$ be stable and regular as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], fix $\beta>0$, and define $Z(L,N;\beta)$ as in that definition. For sequences $L_j\to\infty$ and integers $N_j\geq0$ with $N_j/L_j^d\to\rho$, define
$$b(\rho)=\sup\left\{\limsup_{j\to\infty}L_j^{-d}\log Z(L_j,N_j;\beta):\frac{N_j}{L_j^d}\to\rho\right\}.$$
Let $F$ be the concave envelope of $b$ on $[0,\infty)$, namely the supremum of $\sum_{i=1}^m\theta_i b(\rho_i)$ over finite lists with $\theta_i\geq0$, $\sum_i\theta_i=1$, $\rho_i\geq0$, and $\sum_i\theta_i\rho_i=\rho$; the empty supremum is $-\infty$. On the interior of $\{\rho:F(\rho)>-\infty\}$, $F$ is finite and continuous. For every $\rho>0$ in that interior and every such sequence $(L_j,N_j)$,
$$\lim_{j\to\infty}L_j^{-d}\log Z(L_j,N_j;\beta)=F(\rho).$$
No claim is made at a close-packing endpoint or at any other excluded endpoint.

thm-tdmath-superstable-van-hove-pressure.title: Free-wall pressure on arbitrary van Hove shapes under superstability

thm-tdmath-superstable-van-hove-pressure.statement:
Assume a superstable regular pair potential $\phi$ as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], with stability constant $B$, and the van Hove definition [[def-tdmath-van-hove-sequence]]. For a bounded Lebesgue-measurable $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$, define $\mathcal S_N(\Lambda)=\{(q_1,\ldots,q_N)\in\Lambda^N:q_i\neq q_j\ (i\neq j)\}$ and $H_N(q)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\phi(q_i-q_j)$. With $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$, set
$$Z_\Lambda(N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\mathcal S_N(\Lambda)}e^{-\beta H_N(q)}\,dq_1\cdots dq_N,\qquad Z_\Lambda(0;\beta)=1,\qquad \Xi_\Lambda(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_\Lambda(N;\beta).$$
This is the labelled positional Lebesgue integral with indistinguishable-particle normalization and includes no exterior interaction. For $\Lambda=[0,L)^d$ it agrees with $Z(L,N;\beta)$ and $\Xi(L;z,\beta)$ from [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For every van Hove sequence $(\Omega_k)$ and fixed $z,\beta>0$, the free-wall grand pressure satisfies
$$\lim_{k\to\infty}\frac1{|\Omega_k|}\log\Xi_{\Omega_k}(z,\beta)=p(z,\beta),$$
where $p(z,\beta)$ is the free-cube limit from [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. The extra superstability hypothesis supplies the uniform cell-occupation bound used below; no arbitrary-shape theorem under stability alone is claimed.

thm-tdmath-uniform-tempered-exterior-pre.statement:
Assume a stable regular pair potential $\phi$ as in [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]], with stability constant $B$, and the genuine finite-valued positive-core condition of [[lem-tdmath-superquadratic-positive-core]]: for some $r_0>0$, a nonincreasing $\chi:(0,r_0]\to(0,\infty)$ satisfies $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ for $0<|x|_\infty\leq r_0$ and $\int_0^{r_0}\chi(r)r^{d-1}\,dr=+\infty$. Let $\Lambda_n=[-n-\tfrac12,n+\tfrac12)^d$, $V_n=(2n+1)^d$, $C_i=i+[-\tfrac12,\tfrac12)^d$, and $\mathcal C_{\rm lf}$ be the set of locally finite simple configurations $\zeta\subset\mathbb R^d$. For $t\geq0$ define
$$\Omega(t)=\left\{\zeta\in\mathcal C_{\rm lf}:\sum_{i\in\Lambda_n\cap\mathbb Z^d}N_{C_i}(\zeta)^2\leq tV_n\text{ for every integer }n\geq0\right\}.$$
For $\omega=(q_1,\ldots,q_N)\in\mathcal S_N(\Lambda_n)$, write $H_{n,\mathrm{free}}(\omega)=\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\phi(q_i-q_j)$. For $\zeta\in\Omega(t)$, let $\zeta_n^{\rm out}=\zeta\setminus\Lambda_n$ and define the finite-volume boundary Hamiltonian
$$H_{n,\zeta}(\omega)=H_{n,\mathrm{free}}(\omega)+\sum_{i=1}^N\sum_{y\in\zeta_n^{\rm out}}\phi(q_i-y).$$
The exterior series has finite negative part by the proof below; its extended value may be $+\infty$, with $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$. Define
$$Z_{n,\zeta}(N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\mathcal S_N(\Lambda_n)}e^{-\beta H_{n,\zeta}(\omega)}\,dq_1\cdots dq_N,\qquad Z_{n,\zeta}(0;\beta)=1,\qquad \Xi_{n,\zeta}(z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_{n,\zeta}(N;\beta).$$
For fixed $z,\beta>0$ and $t<\infty$, the free-wall grand pressure with this exterior pair energy satisfies
$$\lim_{n\to\infty}\sup_{\zeta\in\Omega(t)}\left|\frac1{V_n}\log\Xi_{n,\zeta}(z,\beta)-p(z,\beta)\right|=0,$$
where $p(z,\beta)$ is the free-cube pressure from [[thm-tdmath-decreasing-integrable-tail-free-cube-pressure]]. The exterior configuration is restricted to the stated fixed square-count class; no volume-filling external field is included. The conclusion is conditional on the genuine positive core and does not infer it from superstability alone.

thm-tdmath-van-hove-fixed-n-limit.title: Exact canonical limit on arbitrary van Hove shapes

thm-tdmath-van-hove-fixed-n-limit.statement:
Assume superstability and regularity, let $(\Omega_k)$ be van Hove, and let $N_k/|\Omega_k|\to\rho$ for an interior attainable density $\rho>0$. Use the general-region free-wall convention of [[thm-tdmath-superstable-van-hove-pressure]], namely
$$Z(\Lambda,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\{q\in\Lambda^N:q_i\neq q_j\ (i\neq j)\}}\exp\!\left(-\beta\sum_{1\leq i<j\leq N}\phi(q_i-q_j)\right)dq_1\cdots dq_N\quad(N\geq1),$$
with $Z(\Lambda,0;\beta)=1$ and $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$, for bounded Lebesgue-measurable $\Lambda\subset\mathbb R^d$. For the free-wall exact-$N_k$ positional partition with this $1/N_k!$ normalization,
$$|\Omega_k|^{-1}\log Z(\Omega_k,N_k;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho),$$
the free-cube canonical rate of [[thm-tdmath-canonical-interior-density-limit]]. Superstability is used for the arbitrary-shape pressure upper bound; no stability-only upper theorem is asserted.

lem-tdmath-superquadratic-positive-core.title: Superquadratic cell coercivity from a divergent or hard core

lem-tdmath-superquadratic-positive-core.statement:
Assume the potential of [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]] is stable and regular. In addition, assume either (i) $\chi:(0,r_1]\to(0,\infty)$ is finite-valued and nonincreasing, $\phi(x)\geq\chi(|x|_\infty)$ for $0<|x|_\infty\leq r_1$, and $\int_0^{r_1}\chi(r)r^{d-1}dr=+\infty$; or (ii) there is a hard-core radius $r_h>0$ such that $\phi(x)=+\infty$ whenever $|x|_\infty<r_h$. Then there are a nonnegative nondecreasing $h:\mathbb N_0\to[0,+\infty]$ with $h(0)=0$ and $h(N)/N^2\to+\infty$, and a constant $b<\infty$, such that
$$H_\phi(\omega)\geq\sum_{i\in\mathbb Z^d}h(N_{C_i}(\omega))-bN(\omega).$$
The hard-core alternative permits $h(N)=+\infty$ above the finite packing capacity of a unit cell. This is stronger than ordinary superstability and is not inferred from stability or regularity alone.

lem-tdmath-canonical-empirical-field-con.title: Conditioning grand empirical fields on an exact particle number

references.title: H.-O. Georgii, Large deviations and the equivalence of ensembles for Gibbsian particle systems with superstable interaction
references.locator: Theorem 2 and Sections 3–5, printed pp.174–187 / PDF pp.4–17: good large-deviation principle for periodized empirical fields under free or periodic grand-canonical Gibbs laws; complete proof read.

references.locator: Sections 3 and 5: entropy upper bounds, empirical-field tightness, and conditional-law arguments.

lem-tdmath-canonical-empirical-field-con.statement:
Let $\Lambda_L=[0,L)^d$, $\beta,z>0$, and $b\in\{\mathrm{free},\mathrm{per}\}$. On the simple labelled sector $\mathcal S_{L,N}=\{q\in\Lambda_L^N:q_i\neq q_j\ (i\neq j)\}$ use $H_{L,\mathrm{free}}(q)=\sum_{i<j}\phi(q_i-q_j)$ and the periodic energy $H_{L,\mathrm{per}}$ from [[def-tdmath-superstable-regular-interaction]]. For $N\geq1$ define
$$Z_b(L,N;\beta)=\frac1{N!}\int_{\mathcal S_{L,N}}e^{-\beta H_{L,b}(q)}\,dq_1\cdots dq_N,\qquad Z_b(L,0;\beta)=1,$$
with $e^{-\beta(+\infty)}=0$, and put $\Xi_b(L,z,\beta)=\sum_{N\geq0}z^NZ_b(L,N;\beta)$. The unit-intensity Poisson reference $Q_{\Lambda_L}$ has sector density $e^{-L^d}/N!$ relative to labelled Lebesgue measure, so its normalized grand partition is
$$Z_{Q,b}(L;z,\beta)=E_{Q_{\Lambda_L}}[z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,b}}]=e^{-L^d}\Xi_b(L,z,\beta).$$
The exact-$N$ canonical law $C^b_{L,N}$ has density $e^{-\beta H_{L,b}}/(N!Z_b(L,N;\beta))$ on $\mathcal S_{L,N}$, and the grand-canonical law $G^b_{L,z,\beta}$ has density $z^{N_{\Lambda_L}}e^{-\beta H_{L,b}}/Z_{Q,b}(L;z,\beta)$ relative to $Q_{\Lambda_L}$. Let $\rho>0$ be an interior attainable density, choose $\alpha=\log z$ supporting the free canonical rate $F_\beta$ at $\rho$, and take $N_L/L^d\to\rho$. Assume
$$L^{-d}\log Z_b(L,N_L;\beta)\longrightarrow F_\beta(\rho).$$
Let $R_{L,\omega}$ be the periodized empirical field of [[def-tdmath-periodized-empirical-field]], and let
$$\mathcal M_{z,\beta}:=\operatorname*{argmin}_{P\in\mathcal P^1_{\rm stat}}\{I(P)+\beta\Phi(P)-\rho(P)\log z\}.$$
Then for every open $\tau_L$ neighborhood $U$ of $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}$ there is $c_U>0$ such that
$$\limsup_{L\to\infty}L^{-d}\log C^b_{L,N_L}\{\,\omega:R_{L,\omega}\notin U\,\}\leq-c_U.$$
If $\mathcal M_{z,\beta}=\{P_*\}$, then $R_{L,\omega}\to P_*$ in probability in $\tau_L$ under $C^b_{L,N_L}$. This is a statement about spatially averaged local observables through the empirical field, not about the raw finite-box law at a fixed origin.
